People now ask ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Google’s AI answers what they used to search for, and AI assistants increasingly shape the journey from discovery to purchase. Winning customers now means winning over the AI systems that influence their decisions.

Peec AI is an AI search platform that helps marketing teams understand and improve how their brands are discovered, represented, and recommended. We show them where they stand, what’s shaping it, and where to act. Since launching in January 2025, Peec AI has passed $20M ARR and 4,000+ paying customers. We’re a Series A company backed by 20VC and Singular, with 100+ people across our Berlin HQ and our New York office.

About the role

Peec ships something new almost every week. Most customers hear about it late, and some never do. We're hiring a Customer Education Manager to own how customers learn Peec. You'll own the product docs, the changelog, product updates and in-app communication, and turn every release into something a busy marketer understands in a minute.

You'll sit in product marketing and report to our founding product marketer. You'll work every day with product managers and engineers to understand what's shipping, with customer success to see where customers get stuck, and with the growth team to see what actually changes how people use the product.

What you'll do

  • Own the product docs. Rebuild them around the jobs customers come to do, not around the menu. Keep them current with every release, and make them easy to read for people and for the AI assistants our customers now ask first.

  • Run the changelog and product updates. Every release gets a clear entry the day it ships. You write the regular product update and the announcement for bigger launches, and decide what deserves which.

  • Write in-app communication. You write the copy for announcements, tooltips, empty states, onboarding steps and feature nudges. The growth team runs the nudges themselves (who sees what, when, and the tests); you make sure every message is clear, accurate and sounds like one product.

  • Make product content that teaches. Short how-to videos, walkthroughs, use-case guides and templates that get a new user from signup to their first useful insight, and an existing customer to the feature they're missing.

  • Get in early. Sit with product and engineering before launch, early enough to shape naming, setup and the first-run experience, not just document them afterwards.

  • Fix questions at the source. Read support tickets and customer calls, find the questions we keep answering, and make sure the product, docs or messaging answer them before anyone has to ask.

  • Measure what you ship. Track docs usage, support deflection and feature adoption after each update. Keep what works, cut what doesn't.

What we're looking for

  • You come from product. Product management, product ops, technical writing, solutions or support engineering, or customer success with a strong product bent. You learn software deeply by using it and can get a straight answer from a busy engineer.

  • You've owned docs, a help center or release communication for a B2B SaaS product. Show us a before and after.

  • You write simply. You can explain a complex feature in three sentences to someone who has never seen it, and cut a page in half without losing anything. We'll ask for recent work where your part is clear.

  • You like to ship a lot. Many small, useful pieces over one perfect one, and you care as much about keeping them up to date as about publishing them.

  • You're comfortable with data. Given adoption numbers, you can say whether a piece of content worked.

  • You use AI to draft, research and keep content in sync with the product. You build the systems that other teams can plug into to ensure consistency across every touchpoint.

  • You work well across product, engineering, customer success and marketing, make decisions and ship.

Bonus points

  • You built a docs or customer education function from scratch, first in seat.

  • You've worked in martech, SEO, analytics or a data platform, so you already know our customers' world.

  • You make short product videos and screen recordings yourself.

  • You've written in-app messages or product emails in tools like Customer.io, Intercom, Appcues or Pendo.

  • You know how to structure docs so AI assistants read and cite them correctly.

  • You write well in German or French as well as English.

title: Customer Service Agent
descriptionHtml:
Bij Crisp staan onze klanten op nummer één. Ons gezellige en hechte serviceteam doet er alles aan om die klanten van de beste service te voorzien. We hebben daarom veel persoonlijk contact met de klant, en ondersteunen onze bezorgers voor een vlekkeloze bezorging. We zijn nog volop in ontwikkeling, dus je denkt ook mee over hoe we onze service kunnen verbeteren.

Wat je gaat doen

Je hebt elke dag direct contact met onze klanten, vooral via Whatsapp. Zo maak je ze nog blijer nadat ze ons gesproken hebben. Daarnaast geef je feedback van klanten door aan de juiste teams binnen Crisp, zodat we onze service kunnen blijven verbeteren. Ook zorg je samen met onze bezorgers en je collega's op onze logistieke hubs dat bezorgingen vlekkeloos verlopen. Verder verdiep je je in onze processen. Zoals je al hoort, geen dag is hetzelfde!

Hoe ziet een werkdag eruit?

  • 's Ochtends hou je onze bezorgroutes goed in de gaten. Is het druk op de weg? Dan zorg jij ervoor dat onze klanten op tijd weten dat hun bezorger iets later is.

  • Ondertussen pak je WhatsApp-berichtjes van klanten op. Je helpt ze met het aanpassen van hun bestelling, het kiezen van een bezorgtijd of beantwoordt vragen over ons assortiment. Zo leer je elke dag iets nieuws over eten!

  • Lunchtijd! Elke dag lunchen we met onze eigen boodschappen. Een ideaal moment om ons assortiment én je collega's beter te leren kennen.

  • Na de lunch beantwoord je vragen via WhatsApp, social media en e-mail, terwijl je collega's de bezorgingen in de gaten houden of bezig zijn met de processen. Je merkt dat er veel vragen zijn over een bepaalde marketingactie. Dat geef je dus meteen even door aan de juiste collega.

  • De collega's die 's avonds werken nemen jouw taken over. Dat zorgt ervoor dat je de feedback die klanten doorgeven via de app nog even kunt verwerken.

  • Tijd om af te sluiten. Samen met je collega's drink je nog een ijskoud Crisp-drankje in onze gezellige keuken.

Dit ben jij

Je herkent je in het volgende profiel:

  • Je bent parttime (16-24 uur per week) beschikbaar. We zijn 7 dagen per week open van 07:30 tot 23:00 uur, en je werkt straks in shifts van 4 tot 8 uur. Daarom is flexibele beschikbaarheid voor overdag, avonden én in het weekend een must.

  • Je woont in omgeving Amsterdam en bent voor minimaal één jaar beschikbaar.

  • Een kantoor in de Amsterdamse Pijp met een grote keuken waar flink wordt geluncht, gezellig gekookt en waar de kans op zelfgebakken taart of vegan roze koeken groot is. Goed om te weten: vanaf januari 2027 groeien we door en verhuizen we naar een gloednieuwe, grotere locatie in de buurt van Zaandam, Sloterdijk en de Houthavens, waar we vanaf dan onze nieuwe thuisbasis hebben.

  • Je schrijft en spreekt vloeiend Nederlands. Op een persoonlijke en creatieve manier reageren op klanten gaat jou makkelijk af.

  • Je bent oplossingsgericht en empathisch. Je kunt je verplaatsen in onze klanten en begrijpt wat er nodig is om hun ervaring met Crisp nog beter te maken.

  • Je bedenkt creatieve oplossingen om onze klanten te verrassen en verwachtingen te overtreffen.

  • Als je klantenservice-ervaring hebt binnen organisaties waar kwaliteit hoog in het vaandel staat, is dat super!

Wat wij bieden

  • Een marktconform salaris, afhankelijk van leeftijd.

  • Een gezellig en hecht team.

  • Veel verantwoordelijkheid, uitdagend werk en een dynamische omgeving.

  • Een kijkje in de keuken van een snelgroeiende start-up. We zijn volop in ontwikkeling dus jouw ideeën tellen mee.

  • Werken bij een B-Corp gecertificeerd bedrijf, waarbij je de kans krijgt om je stempel te drukken op ons voedselsysteem en échte verandering teweeg te brengen

  • Enthousiaste en ondernemende collega’s om mee te werken en te leren.

  • Voor straks een perfect pensioen via BPFL.

  • Voor nu een persoonlijk budget voor yoga, sport, mobiliteit en downtime via bijvoorbeeld ClassPass, Pathé en Blendle.

  • Elke maand food for thought, met workshops en talks via de Crisp University.

  • Tijd om je collega’s te leren kennen tijdens sport, events en proeverijen.

  • Een kantoor in de Amsterdamse Pijp met een grote keuken waar flink wordt geluncht, gezellig gekookt en grote kans op zelfgebakken taart of vegan roze koeken.

  • En... fikse korting op je Crisp boodschappen, omdat je thuis natuurlijk ook goed wilt eten.

Ben jij geïnteresseerd?

Is de functie van Service Agent jou op het lijf geschreven, solliciteer dan via onderstaand button. Hoe meer je kunt delen over jezelf en de reden dat je solliciteert, hoe beter.

Bij Crisp streven we naar een inclusieve en diverse werkomgeving waarin iedereen welkom is, ongeacht hun achtergrond, geslacht, leeftijd, etniciteit, seksuele geaardheid, religie of beperking. Wij moedigen sollicitanten met diverse perspectieven en achtergronden aan om te solliciteren en geloven in gelijke kansen voor iedereen. We waarderen de unieke bijdragen die elke medewerker kan leveren en zijn vastbesloten om een inclusieve werkplek te creëren waarin iedereen wordt gerespecteerd en gewaardeerd.

About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The Role

As a Defense Success Manager, you own what happens to our most strategic defense and sovereign accounts after the build: you make deployed AI stick in real workflows — often in restricted or disconnected environments — keep production commitments healthy, defend renewals, and source the expansion signals that Sales closes.

Mistral's Solutions teams (Deployment Strategists and Forward Deployed Engineers) co-create high-value AI use cases with customers in these environments. Your job is to make those investments successful beyond delivery — adopting what has been built, operating it with confidence, demonstrating its impact, and scaling value across the institution. You will work with mission owners, program stakeholders, end users, security and IT teams, and across Mistral with Solutions, Product, Engineering and Support.

This is not a high-volume, ticket-queue customer success role. Portfolios are small and deep — typically one or two flagship accounts plus a small number of adjacent programs. It calls for a strategic account mindset, the technical judgment to navigate complex and constrained deployment environments, and the energy to build the customer success function as Mistral grows. Travel to customer sites, including secure facilities, is a regular part of the job.

You will join on one of two tracks (and can move between them):

  • Adoption track — embedded in flagship programs while Solutions is still delivering. You own the adoption and change-management motion around the build: user waves, enablement, champions, training programs, and the evidence that proves value is landing.

  • Operational track — you take accounts through a structured handover once Solutions completes delivery, and own the run phase end-to-end: operational health, value realization, renewals, and expansion signals.

In both tracks you operate in close partnership with Solutions: they deliver and hand over; you own post-handover; they re-engage on expansion signals. Occasionally, account teams will also pull you into late-stage pre-sales — authoring the customer training and scale-up plan that gives a buyer confidence in the rollout.


What You Will Do


Own the customer success and value plan

  • Build a clear view of each account's objectives, stakeholders, deployed use cases, commitments and risks. Translate it into a shared success plan with owners, milestones and measurable outcomes.

  • Establish a practical operating cadence with customer sponsors, business owners, IT and delivery teams. Lead success reviews that make progress, risks, decisions and next steps clear.

  • Define a baseline and track the outcomes that matter for each use case: adoption and usage against entitled seats, customer satisfaction, operational health and business impact. Turn the evidence into a clear value narrative.

Make deployment realities part of the success plan

  • Understand how each customer's deployment model — on-premises, VPC or serverless — affects the products and use cases they can access, operate and scale. Validate the specifics with the technical teams rather than assuming feature parity or identical operating models.

  • Identify the practical implications of deployment choices: security and data requirements, access and integrations, release and upgrade cadence, available features, capacity, observability and support processes. Explain the trade-offs clearly to customer and Mistral stakeholders.

  • Translate those constraints into an actionable adoption plan: align enablement and release communications with the version the customer actually runs, account for security approvals and upgrade windows, and agree how to measure usage when telemetry is limited.

  • Spot risks early, qualify their impact on adoption, renewal or value, and coordinate the right Solutions, Product, Engineering or Support owners to resolve them. Set clear expectations without making unvalidated technical or roadmap commitments.

Drive adoption, autonomy and sustained value

  • Help customer teams move from a delivered use case to regular, effective use. Identify the users, workflows and change-management needs that determine whether it sticks.

  • Coordinate onboarding, training, product updates and hands-on enablement with the right Mistral and customer teams. Develop customer champions and train-the-trainer motions so adoption scales beyond direct Mistral involvement.

  • Prepare the transition from delivery to run: clarify operational ownership, support and escalation paths, and the resources users need to succeed independently.

  • Monitor adoption and customer health, investigate where usage or value is falling short, and lead a coordinated plan to address the causes.

Defend and grow the commercial relationship

  • Own the renewal motion for your accounts: know every renewal date, the auto vs non-auto renewal terms, and the risk story behind each one. Run the renewal play early — no surprises at renewal time.

  • Track and improve account NRR. Identify new use cases, teams and expansion opportunities, and share them with the account team grounded in demonstrated value.

  • Lead business reviews with the account team: value delivered, risks owned, decisions needed, roadmap asks.

Bring the customer voice into Mistral

  • Gather and qualify feedback from users, technical teams and sponsors. Distinguish enablement needs from product gaps, deployment constraints and support issues, and route each to the right owner.

  • Track important requests and communicate progress and limitations back to the customer, while Product and Engineering retain ownership of product and technical decisions.

Build the company as well as the account

  • Create the playbooks, success plans, handover practices and measurement approaches that are missing. Test them with customers, improve them, and make them reusable across accounts.

  • Bring structure to ambiguity: identify what needs to happen, make a plan, mobilize the right people and follow through — without waiting for a perfect process or detailed instructions.

  • Roughly a fifth of your time is protected, rotating build time for exactly this work; it is part of the job, not extra to it.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years of experience owning outcomes for enterprise or institutional customers of technical products or deployed solutions — adoption and commercial outcomes (retention, renewal, expansion), not relationship management or activity reporting.

  • Strong technical fluency in secure enterprise deployment models. You can identify what a deployment type (on-premise, disconnected, air-gapped) means for available features, telemetry, upgrades and accreditation, and you validate specifics with technical teams instead of assuming parity.

  • Ability to engage credibly with architects, engineers, IT and security stakeholders, while translating technical trade-offs into clear implications for mission owners and executives. You know when to bring in a deeper technical expert.

  • Comfort operating under security, compliance and confidentiality constraints, including restricted or classified environments and strict information-handling rules.

  • Strong ownership and builder energy. You have created structure or improved a process in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment and are motivated to build a company, not wait for clear directions.

  • Excellent communication, stakeholder management and execution skills. You align teams without formal authority, surface risks early and drive decisions through to completion

  • Analytical and commercially minded: you can define meaningful success metrics with imperfect data, assess customer health, and are comfortable carrying renewal and NRR accountability.


Nice to have

  • Experience serving defense, public sector or critical infrastructure customers, including sovereign or classified programs.

  • Experience with AI, machine learning, data platforms or complex enterprise software, including production deployments in regulated or security-sensitive environments.

  • Experience working alongside deployment, engineering or professional services teams on custom use cases, and the transition from implementation to ongoing operation.

  • Familiarity with public procurement, framework agreements and multi-year option structures.

Security & Compliance criteria

  • Eligibility: must hold citizenship in the target territory (France for now).

  • Clearable: must meet all local requirements for high-level security clearance (e.g. no criminal record, fulfillment of national service obligations).

What We Offer

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page.

Privacy Policy

Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy.

title: Deine studienintegrierte Ausbildung: Fachinformatiker (m/w/d) und Informatik B.Sc.
descriptionHtml:
Studienintegrierende Ausbildung zum Fachinformatiker (m/w/d) für Systemintegration mit Bachelorstudium Informatik (B.Sc.)

Dein Einstieg in die IT: Theorie verstehen, Praxis erleben, Zukunft gestalten.

Du interessierst dich für Informatik, möchtest technische Zusammenhänge verstehen und hast Freude daran, Lösungen für knifflige Aufgaben zu finden? Gleichzeitig möchtest du nicht nur theoretisch lernen, sondern dein Wissen von Anfang an in der Praxis anwenden?

Dann könnte unsere studienintegrierende Ausbildung genau das Richtige für dich sein.

Bei der Deutschen Extrakt Kaffee GmbH (DEK) verbindest du eine Ausbildung zum Fachinformatiker (m/w/d) für Systemintegration mit einem Bachelorstudium der Informatik an der Beruflichen Hochschule Hamburg (BHH).

In Zusammenarbeit mit der BHH bieten wir dir die Möglichkeit, innerhalb von vier Jahren einen anerkannten Berufsabschluss und den akademischen Abschluss Bachelor of Science (B.Sc.) zu erwerben.

Dabei lernst du unsere IT-Systeme und digitalen Prozesse kennen, sammelst praktische Erfahrungen und vertiefst gleichzeitig dein theoretisches Wissen.

So verbindest du das Beste aus Ausbildung und Studium und legst eine vielseitige Grundlage für deine berufliche Zukunft.

Das erwartet dich in deiner studienintegrierenden Ausbildung

Bei uns lernst du die IT eines international tätigen Unternehmens kennen und erfährst, wie technische Systeme miteinander verbunden sind und im Arbeitsalltag eingesetzt werden.

Dabei wechselst du zwischen drei Lernorten: unserem Unternehmen, der Berufsschule und der Beruflichen Hochschule Hamburg (BHH).

Das bedeutet für dich:

  • Du lernst unsere IT-Welt kennen: Von Computern und Netzwerken über Server bis hin zu komplexeren IT-Systemen erfährst du, wie unsere technische Infrastruktur aufgebaut ist und zusammenarbeitet.

  • Du verbindest Theorie und Praxis: An der BHH beschäftigst du dich mit den wissenschaftlichen Grundlagen der Informatik, während du dein Wissen bei uns im Unternehmen praktisch anwenden und vertiefen kannst.

  • Du bringst Technik zum Laufen: Du unterstützt bei der Einrichtung, Betreuung und Weiterentwicklung unserer IT-Systeme und lernst, wie wir für einen zuverlässigen IT-Betrieb sorgen.

  • Du gehst Problemen auf den Grund: Du analysierst technische Störungen, suchst nach Ursachen und entwickelst gemeinsam mit deinem Team passende Lösungen.

  • Du beschäftigst dich mit IT-Sicherheit: Du erfährst, wie wir unsere Systeme, Netzwerke und Daten schützen und welche Bedeutung IT-Sicherheit für unser Unternehmen hat.

  • Du gestaltest digitale Lösungen mit: Du lernst unsere IT-Prozesse kennen und kannst dich in Projekte einbringen, mit denen wir unsere technische Infrastruktur und digitale Arbeitsabläufe weiterentwickeln.

  • Du wächst mit deinen Aufgaben: Mit zunehmendem Wissen und Erfahrung übernimmst du eigene Aufgaben und entwickelst dich fachlich und persönlich weiter.

Ausbildung und Studium: So funktioniert das Modell

Mit der studienintegrierenden Ausbildung bieten wir dir gemeinsam mit der Beruflichen Hochschule Hamburg (BHH) einen Bildungsweg, der berufliche Praxis und akademisches Lernen miteinander verbindet.

Das Besondere: Ausbildung und Studium laufen nicht einfach unabhängig voneinander ab, sondern sind inhaltlich und organisatorisch aufeinander abgestimmt.

Während deiner vierjährigen Ausbildungs- und Studienzeit lernst du an drei unterschiedlichen Orten:

  • Bei uns im Unternehmen: Du sammelst praktische Erfahrungen, lernst unsere IT-Abteilung kennen und arbeitest an betrieblichen Aufgaben und Projekten mit.

  • In der Berufsschule: Du erwirbst die beruflichen Fachkenntnisse, die du für deine Ausbildung zum Fachinformatiker (m/w/d) für Systemintegration benötigst.

  • An der BHH: Du vertiefst dein Wissen im Bachelorstudiengang Informatik und beschäftigst dich unter anderem mit Programmierung, Mathematik, Softwareentwicklung und IT-Sicherheit.

Die Lernphasen sind aufeinander abgestimmt, sodass du dein Wissen aus den unterschiedlichen Bereichen miteinander verbinden kannst.

Am Ende kannst du gleich zwei Abschlüsse in der Tasche haben: deinen Berufsabschluss als Fachinformatiker (m/w/d) für Systemintegration und den Bachelor of Science (B.Sc.) in Informatik.

Das bringst du mit

Du möchtest Informatik studieren, gleichzeitig praktische Erfahrungen sammeln und verstehen, wie IT-Lösungen im Unternehmensalltag eingesetzt werden? Dann bringst du schon eine wichtige Voraussetzung mit.

Was uns außerdem wichtig ist:

  • Du hast die (Fach-)Hochschulreife oder stehst kurz vor deinem Abschluss und erfüllst die Zugangsvoraussetzungen der BHH.

  • Du interessierst dich für Informatik, digitale Technologien und technische Zusammenhänge.

  • Du hast Freude daran, logisch zu denken, Zusammenhänge zu erkennen und Lösungen für knifflige Aufgaben zu finden.

  • Du beschäftigst dich gerne mit neuen Themen und bringst die Motivation mit, dich sowohl im Studium als auch in der Praxis weiterzuentwickeln.

  • Du arbeitest gerne mit anderen zusammen, bist offen für neue Ideen und scheust dich nicht, Fragen zu stellen.

  • Du kannst dich gut organisieren und bist bereit, die Anforderungen von Ausbildung und Studium miteinander zu verbinden.

Du musst noch kein IT-Profi sein. Erste Erfahrungen mit Computern oder Programmierung sind natürlich hilfreich, aber viel wichtiger sind uns dein Interesse an Informatik, deine Lernbereitschaft und die Freude daran, Neues auszuprobieren.

Unser Angebot

  • Bei uns kannst du Ausbildung und Privatleben super verbinden! Dank unserer Gleitzeitregelung hast du die Möglichkeit, deinen Arbeitstag flexibel zu gestalten – so lassen sich Familie, Freizeit und Beruf optimal miteinander vereinbaren.

  • Bei uns startest du im ersten Lehrjahr mit 1.284€ brutto. Dies erhöht sich im zweiten Lehrjahr auf 1.342€ brutto und im dritten Lehrjahr auf 1.412€ brutto. Zusätzlich bieten wir Dir Urlaubsgeld, Weihnachtsgeld und jährliche Gehaltsanpassungen.

  • Unsere Idee ist, dass du nach der Ausbildung bei uns bleibst: Du erhältst eine strukturierte Einarbeitung und eine praxisnahe Ausbildung. So hast du die besten Chancen, nach deiner Ausbildung übernommen zu werden und langfristig mit uns gemeinsam zu wachsen.

  • Karriere mit Geschmack: Du erhältst monatliche Freikontingente, damit Du auch nach der Arbeit erstklassigen Kaffee oder Kakao genießen kannst.

  • Unsere Mitarbeitenden liegen uns am Herzen, u.a. mit Geburtstags- und Weihnachtsgeschenken machen wir Dir regelmäßig eine Freude.

  • Wir bieten Dir weitere Benefits wie unsere betriebseigene Kantine, in der täglich frisch gekocht wird, eine Übernahme des Deutschlandtickets, betriebliche Altersvorsorge, vergünstigte Sport- und Gesundheitsangebote über machtfit und ein professionelles Mental Health Angebot durch das Fürstenberg Institut.

Dürfen wir uns kurz vorstellen?

Familiär. International. Langfristig.

Besondere Qualität entsteht, wenn Tradition und Moderne miteinander harmonieren.

Wir gehen respektvoll, offen und hilfsbereit miteinander um und geben jeden Tag unser Bestes, um erstklassige Kaffee-Spezialitäten zu produzieren.

Bei der DEK arbeiten Sie in einem internationalen Umfeld und spüren zugleich die Vorteile eines inhabergeführten Familienunternehmens.

Kontakt

Ihre Ansprechpartnerin


Haben Sie Fragen zur Position oder zum Bewerbungsverfahren? Wenden Sie sich gerne an Jennifer Brunsiek unter 040 75304 394 oder per E-Mail:

Wir freuen uns über geeignete Bewerbungen unabhängig von Geschlecht, kultureller und sozialer Herkunft, Alter, Religion, Weltanschauung, Behinderung oder sexueller Identität.

Deutsche Extrakt Kaffee GmbH - Cafeastraße 1 - 21107 Hamburg

title: Delivery Manager
descriptionHtml:
Delivery Manager


Location: Our offices are in Central London, along with several of our customers. Travel to our customer sites is required, the frequency of which will vary from customer-to-customer. You need to be able to travel onsite to London up to 3 days per week, although onsite requirements will vary week-to-week and customer-to-customer from 0 to 3 days.

Salary: £45,000 - £80,000

SC Clearance Requirements:

Due to working with several government bodies, SC clearance is required for all our customer facing teams. You do not need active SC clearance as we will undertake checks upon you joining, but you must be eligible to pass SC clearance. In future, DV clearance may be required, so the ability/willingness to pass DV clearance is advantageous but not essential.

You must be UK-based.


About us

We are experts in building central cloud platforms, cloud risk mitigation and cloud operating models, providing thought leadership to central government and private enterprise organisations to help them unlock the true value of cloud.

 

Why you should join us

At Cloudscaler, you'll be part of a consultancy at the forefront of cloud transformation, trusted by government, defence, and enterprise organisations to deliver complex AWS solutions that make a real national impact. From modernising public services to securing critical infrastructure, the work you do will matter far beyond technology.

We combine the agility of a startup with the credibility of an AWS Advanced Partner, creating a high-trust, high-performance culture where self-starters thrive and every voice is heard. You'll work closely with senior leadership and cloud experts, shaping meaningful projects and driving innovation.

By joining us, you'll accelerate your personal and professional development through hands-on experience with cutting-edge cloud solutions. You'll learn directly from experts while contributing to some of the UK's most ambitious cloud programmes, gaining exposure and influence you wouldn't find in a larger consultancy.

 

About the role

Cloudscaler is growing. We are winning more cloud engagements across public and private sector, and we need delivery professionals who can take ownership of engagements and see them through. This role exists to make sure our client work is delivered on time, within scope, and to the standard that has built our reputation. You will report to the Chief Delivery Officer and work alongside Lead and Senior Delivery Managers across Cloudscaler’s client portfolio.

The role is client-facing and hands-on. It suits someone who has already delivered a complex technology programme end to end and wants to grow their consulting and stakeholder skills in a supportive team.

 

What we're looking for

  • Experience delivering at complex technology-led programme end to end. Datacentre migration, infrastructure or cloud transformation is preferred over generic programme management.

  • Hands-on experience producing delivery reporting and artefacts (status reports, RAID logs, plans and roadmaps) using tooling such as Jira, Confluence or equivalent.

  • Experience in a consulting environment, or an internal role with a strong client-facing delivery element.

  • Confident working with client stakeholders; you can run a project meeting, influence people who do not report to you, and have honest conversations about scope, timeline or risk, knowing when to escalate.

  • Experience delivering AWS-based engagements; hands-on AWS experience is not essential provided you understand core cloud infrastructure concepts.

  • Experience working in or running agile delivery teams (Scrum, Kanban or hybrid).

  • Experience of public sector delivery and familiarity with government digital service standards.

  • Understanding of cloud migration approaches and the delivery challenges involved in moving and modernising workloads.

  • Some exposure to pre-sales, estimation or scoping work.

  • Relevant qualifications are a plus but not essential: PRINCE2, AgilePM, Scrum Master, AWS Cloud Practitioner or equivalent.

 

Benefits

  • Discretionary bonus

  • Discretionary security clearance bonus for those holding certain clearance

  • Periodic offer of share options schemes

  • 25 days’ annual leave

  • 5 additional days per year towards training, certifications, or charity work

  • Option to buy additional annual leave up to 5 days per year

  • Public holidays opt-out scheme, the option to work on public holidays creating the flexibility to enjoy your time off when it suits you

  • Certifications and training expensed

  • Life Assurance

  • Long Term Disability cover

  • Employee Assist Programme for employee advice and support (including legal and counselling helpline)

  • Health, Mental Health, Wellbeing, Financial and Legal support

  • 24/7 GP access

  • Pension auto-enrolment and contribution

  • Employee referral scheme

  • Client referral scheme

  • Cycle to work scheme

  • Travel expenses policy

 

Interview Process

  • Screening call with our Talent Acquisition team

  • 1st Interview - 30 minute remote interview with our hiring team

  • 2nd Interview - 60 minute remote Scenario based interview with members of our Delivery team

  • 3rd Interview - 60 minute in person interview with members of our Senior Leadership Team

If you would like to join us on our adventure, please apply!

Cloudscaler are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, committed to equal opportunities regardless of gender identity, sexual orientation, race, ancestry, age, marital status, disability, parental status, religion or medical history.

If you require reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process or within the workplace, please let us know when you speak to our Talent Acquisition team or contact

title: Design System Lead
descriptionHtml:
Design System Lead

Location: Bristol/London, UK (hybrid, three days a week in the office)
Team: UX
Contract: Permanent
Reporting To: Head of UX

Please note: This role requires an existing right to work in the UK. We can’t offer visa sponsorship, but we review sponsorship role by role, so keep an eye on our careers site for future opportunities


About Kaluza

Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future.

Our platform orchestrates millions of real-time decisions across homes, devices, markets and grids. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable, affordable and adaptive to everyday life.

With teams across Europe, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen.


What you’ll do

  • Shape the future of the design system and the global Agent Experience product as an equal partner to engineering, product, and delivery

  • Create and deliver the design strategy for the system in direct partnership with the engineering lead, holding joint accountability for its direction

  • Set and uphold the design and UX quality bar across every contribution, including accessibility, comfortable challenging engineers and designers alike, and being challenged in return

  • Run the contribution process end to end, so teams beyond our own can propose, design, and ship into the system, from first proposal through to full adoption

  • Design, prototype, and ship components yourself, including using AI-assisted tools to move from Figma to production code, built to WCAG 2.2 AA from the start

  • Coach and develop the designers and engineers who build with the system, raising the bar for how people use and contribute to it

  • Represent the design system to stakeholders across the business, advocating for its value and shaping how the wider company understands and invests in it

  • Champion good design and accessibility thinking in architecture and technical decisions, working alongside senior engineering leaders as a peer

What you’ll bring
Ideally you’ll have/be

  • Deep experience designing, building, and evolving a design system at scale, tokens, component APIs, documentation, and governance

  • Strong design and UX judgement, starting from the user, with genuine comfort challenging and being challenged by engineers and other designers

  • Practical knowledge of WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility standards, with real empathy for designing for users with accessibility needs, not just compliance

  • Confidence working in code, using AI-assisted tools to take a component from design intent through to shipped reality

  • Experience running a contribution or change process across multiple teams or apps, from proposal to full migration

  • A track record setting and delivering technical and design strategy jointly with engineering, iteratively, through genuine ambiguity, not from a finished plan

  • Strong communication skills, able to hold your opinions loosely, and to raise what matters even when it’s inconvenient, across engineering, product, and the wider business

  • Experience mentoring, coaching, and developing other designers

  • A bias to action, comfortable building momentum in the face of real uncertainty

Where you'll work

We offer flexible working, with an expectation of 3 days a week in the office. This gives us the best of both: real time together to collaborate and build relationships, with the flexibility to work in the way that suits you best the rest of the week.


Our Values

  • Play to win: Collective pride in decarbonising energy at scale.

  • Solve the real problem: Cutting through complexity to focus on real-world outcomes.

  • Build trust every day: Consistency, transparency and doing what we say.

  • Own the outcome: Full accountability, wins and setbacks, without ego.

  • Go further together: Collaboration, respect and different perspectives.

Our Perks

  • Time off and family: 26 days’ holiday, plus 26 weeks’ full pay for new parents with no qualifying service period

  • Health and security: Private medical insurance with virtual GP, life assurance, pension scheme, free mortgage advice and eye tests

  • Pay and flexibility: Discretionary bonus, a Flex Fund of 5% [of salary] to spend on the benefits you want most, retail discounts through Perks at Work

  • Growth and setup: Personal learning budget, home office budget

  • Climate: Furthr, our climate action app

Come as you are

We want to meet people from all walks of life. The more inclusive we are, the better our work will be, and we recognise talent on merit and potential. If you’re excited about the role but don’t tick every box, we’d still love to hear from you.

Find out more on our careers page and LinkedIn. Our Applicant Data Protection Policy is here.

title: Developer Community Lead
descriptionHtml:
About RhymeQ

RhymeQ is on a mission to make quantum programmable for every developer. Today, developing quantum software often requires deep physics expertise and code tailored to specific hardware. We’re removing these barriers so developers can focus on solving problems.

Headquartered in Karlsruhe, Germany, we bring together an international team with an open mindset, an energetic team spirit, and a shared drive to build something that matters. We value initiative, ownership, and collaboration, giving everyone the space to contribute ideas, take responsibility, and help shape the future of quantum programming.

Your role

As our Developer Community Lead, you will help developers discover, write their first quantum program, and keep building. Your goal is to turn early interest into an active community where developers learn from one another, share projects, and contribute to the product’s development.

You will combine technical education, community building, and developer outreach. Working closely with our founders and engineering team, you will shape the community experience and grow the community internationally to our target size.

What you will do

  • Grow an active developer community: Build relationships with universities, programming communities, quantum organizations, and event organizers to attract developers to RHYME.
  • Help newcomers succeed: Create a clear onboarding journey, from registration and installation to running and sharing a first quantum program.
  • Build reasons to return: Organize onboarding cohorts, office hours, coding challenges, and hackathons that encourage continued learning and participation.
  • Create useful technical content: Develop tutorials, sample projects, livestreams, posts, and talks that make quantum programming approachable.
  • Support community contributions: Encourage developers to share their work, answer questions, and help others. Identify and support potential community ambassadors.
  • Connect developers with the product team: Turn questions, feedback, and recurring problems into clear recommendations for the compiler, tooling, and documentation.
  • Measure what works: Track acquisition, activation, retention, and contributions, and use the results to improve community programs.

What you bring

  • Bachelor’s in computer science, PhD is preferred.
  • Over 2 years of experience growing a developer community for a technical product, with results you can demonstrate through active users, downloads, contributors, event participation, or other relevant measures.
  • Practical Python skills. You can run code examples, lead a live tutorial, and help a newcomer troubleshoot their setup.
  • The ability to explain technical concepts clearly and make learning engaging, whether in writing, on camera, or on stage.
  • Strong written and spoken English and confidence working with an international audience.
  • A self-driven approach: you can set priorities, organize programs, deliver them, and learn from the results.
  • An open, supportive communication style that helps developers feel comfortable asking questions and sharing unfinished work.
  • An understanding of quantum computing fundamentals, or the motivation to learn them quickly.

Your ability to build trust with developers, teach through code, and grow sustained participation matters most.

What we offer

  • Ownership from the start: Shape our community strategy, programs, and developer experience as our first community hire.
  • Direct collaboration with the founders: Work closely with the people building RHYME and bring developer needs into product decisions.
  • An open, international team: Share ideas, experiment, and learn alongside colleagues who value initiative and collaboration.
  • Visible impact: Help developers move from curiosity about quantum computing to building their own applications.
  • Remote work within Europe.

Help Build Europe's Hypersonic Capability At Hypersonica, we’re redefining what’s possible in European defence technology. We exist to deliver speed, resilience, and technological independence at a pace that sets a new standard. We are a small, elite team working on problems that matter, and solving them fast. By joining Hypersonica, you’re not stepping into a predefined role. You’re joining a talent dense environment where every individual shapes the direction of the company. Our philosophy is to hire a small number of exceptional people with broad, deep technical capability, strong judgement, and the ability to operate autonomously. We hire for talent, not rigid boxes. This role represents a business need, but the way it evolves will be shaped by the individual. If you’ve achieved what others said was impossible, or you bring a unique combination of skills that doesn’t fit a traditional mould, we want to hear from you. The work you do here directly contributes to Europe’s technological independence.

Getting complex hardware through development and into flight is one challenge. Building the industrial capability to deliver it repeatedly, at the required quality and rate, is another. We’re looking for a Director of Industrialisation to lead that work in Germany.

You’ll take a greenfield manufacturing site from an empty floor to sustained series production. You’ll shape the facility, decide what we build in-house, bring in the equipment and people, and lead the ramp until the operation can deliver reliably. Your job starts while the product is still taking shape, when the right manufacturing decision can save months of work later.

We’re looking for someone who’s done this before and wants to build again. You’ll work directly with the founders and with Engineering, Programmes, Quality, Supply Chain and Operations. You’ll be close enough to the floor to see where the plan is breaking down, and senior enough to make the decisions that fix it.


What you’ll do

  • Own the industrialisation plan. Translate programme demand into a plan for capacity, capital investment, people and suppliers. Set milestones from facility readiness through pilot builds and production ramp, and make the trade-offs visible when timelines or assumptions change.

  • Build and commission the operation. Define what the site needs to support, shape the layout and material flow, and lead equipment selection, installation and commissioning. Plan how the operation will expand as demand grows.

  • Bring manufacturing into product decisions early. Work with Engineering to make the hardware practical to build, inspect and test. Bring evidence from the floor into design reviews, and agree how changes will be introduced as the design matures.

  • Decide what to make and what to buy. Work with Supply Chain to establish which capabilities we need to own, where specialist suppliers make sense, and how we qualify and scale those suppliers alongside our own production.

  • Take pilot builds into repeatable production. Use early builds to expose what will limit output. Resolve bottlenecks, improve yield and build consistency, and demonstrate that the operation can sustain its target rate across successive builds.

  • Build the team and the way it works. Hire the people who will establish the operation. Give them clear ownership, develop leaders on the floor, and put in place the training and routines that let the team solve problems as production grows.

  • Own manufacturing readiness. Define the evidence needed before increasing the rate, from process capability and trained operators to supplier readiness, inspection and traceability. Work with Quality and Safety to build those requirements into everyday work.

  • Make the hard calls. Decide where automation earns its place, where a simpler process gets us there sooner, and where to commit capital before all the answers are in. Give leadership a clear view of what’s on track, what’s at risk and what decision is needed.


    • Who you are

  • You’ve personally led a greenfield site or a major production operation built from scratch, through commissioning and into sustained series or volume production. You can tell us what existed on day one, what you owned and what the operation was delivering once it ramped.

  • You’ve industrialised complex hardware while the design was still evolving. You know how to keep engineering and manufacturing moving together when a design change affects tooling, suppliers, inspection or the delivery plan.

  • You’ve made consequential capital, capacity and staffing decisions. You can explain what you committed to early, what you deliberately kept flexible and how those choices played out.

  • You’ve lived through a difficult ramp. You can talk us through a target you missed, how you found the real constraint, what you changed and what happened to output, yield, cost or delivery as a result.

  • You’ve built and led teams across disciplines. You can earn the trust of operators, technicians and engineers, challenge a design decision with evidence, and explain a manufacturing trade-off to the founders in plain language.

  • You know how to build at pace in a demanding hardware environment. You put the controls that matter in place early, and keep decisions close to the people doing the work.

  • You’re motivated by the opportunity to build industrial capability for European defence, and you want to be on site with the team doing it.


    • Where you might have done it
    You might have launched a new factory in automotive, built a production operation at a hardware startup, or taken an aerospace or advanced manufacturing product from low-rate builds to series production. You could have done it inside a larger company if you had the mandate to build the operation and were personally accountable for the ramp.The common thread is the build itself. We want to hear about the operation you created, how quickly you brought it online, the rate it sustained and the decisions you made when the original plan met reality.
    What we offer

  • Genuine ownership of the industrialisation of one of Europe’s most ambitious defence engineering programmes, from an empty site to sustained series production.

  • The chance to join early enough that your decisions will shape the factory, the team and how Hypersonica manufactures for years to come.

  • Direct access to the founders and the factory floor, with short decision paths and the authority to act when you see a better way to build.

  • Daily collaboration with exceptional people across Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Test and Programmes. You’ll have a seat at the table while the product is still taking shape.

  • The freedom to challenge convention and build from first principles, from what we make in-house to where automation earns its place.

  • The resources and ambition to build a production operation at a pace that would be hard to match in a traditional aerospace organisation.

  • The chance to see your decisions through, from the first factory layout on a whiteboard to hardware coming off a line that delivers reliably, shift after shift.

    • At Hypersonica, every hire raises the bar. We are deliberately small, intensely capable, and deeply mission-driven. If this role feels like a strong fit, or if you believe you bring something exceptional that goes beyond the description, we encourage you to apply. Hypersonica is an equal-opportunity employer and assesses candidates solely on merit, capability, and potential. You can apply directly to this role or reach out to Nathan Sweeney, Head of Talent. We review every application and aim to respond to all candidates within two weeks, whether the answer is yes or no.

title: Director of Talent Acquisition at United Media
descriptionHtml:
Do you thrive in a fast-paced environment, where you gain a tremendous amount of responsibility? Do you want to be part of an exceptional entrepreneurial team with motivated and extremely driven people? And are you curious or passionate about people? If so, you might be our next Director of Talent Acquisition.

About us

United Media focuses on building large scale industry media and conferences products in sectors such as insurance, HR, private equity, retail, etc. As of today, we have organically launched 8 media companies and acquired one. (Insurtech Insights, Presidents Summit, Private Equity Insights, HRtechX, CFO insights, Retail Insights and SetSales)

What we offer you

As our Director of Talent Acquisition, you get the unique opportunity to be a key player in building the greatest brand within Insurtech. By providing you with the ownership of our recruiting, we want to constantly push you out of your comfort zone ensuring you become an expert. You’ll be working out of our HQ in London and to ensure a never-ending growth curve, we provide you with:

  • An opportunity for getting operational experience in a start-up where both your work and the results are highly tangible and matters to the business
  • A chance to work closely together with the CEO on our recruiting strategy
  • Unlimited growth potential in our company - we strongly believe in and have a track record of promoting internally

Watch this video with our founder to learn more about our thoughts on recruiting.

Your Responsibilities

Your responsibilities will vary; however, some of them will be to:

  • Take ownership of all aspects of the recruitment process, including; role profiling, candidate sourcing, CV screening, assessment planning, creating interview scripts and conducting interviews
  • Build a strong employer brand and attracting both the obvious talents (what we call shouting talents) as well as the more covert talents (what we call whispering talents)
  • Own the execution of further developing and automating our recruiting processes
  • Improve our onboarding process in close collaboration with management

What we expect from you

We expect that you take ownership of everything you do, are proactive and follow through on commitments. You possess an unparalleled work ethic with a high sense of urgency. You have a relentless drive and desire to be the very best at what you do. Moreover, you are humble and you share our passion for building and executing new businesses. While we have no preferences as to whether you have a background in HR, marketing, sales, or something completely different, we expect that you have an innate desire to get to know other people and learn, develop, and push yourself. If need be, we will teach you everything you need to know about recruiting. We do expect you to:

  • Work experience with outstanding performance 
  • Have an UK work permit
  • Be curious and have a genuine and deep passion for working with and understanding people
  • Want to spend your day speaking with people ranging from students to executives
  • Have a natural ability to make people feel comfortable around you

Startdate

Flexible

Monday - Friday we work from our office (next to Victoria Station) and do not offer remote work.

3594 - Director, Planning - UK

The planning team are the guardians of creating industry leading, unrivalled work at Wavemaker. We are central conduits to all specialists, striving to push boundaries and have a positive impact on consumers and brand.

Wavemaker UK is looking for a Director, Planning to join our growing planning team, to drive forward our planning output and help to create amazing work for our clients.

In this role, you will:

Media Planning Craft:

Effective communication:

  • Manage senior client relationships, understanding what they need for their business and how to drive growth for them.

Idea creation and storytelling:

  • Have an advanced commercial understanding of Wavemakers products and services. Understanding which are suitable for their clients and how sell in solutions.
  • Be a story telling expert, driving added value with the team and quality boosting output.

Skills and Experience

Practice Area Knowledge – Advanced- Demonstrates advanced understanding of the industry as well as future trends Serves as an internal consultant/expert on at least some tools and technology.

Effectively guides junior team members on advanced elements.

Works with leadership team to develop new solutions and/or spot new applications

Problem Solving – Advanced - Performs complex analyses of a range of information and identifies issues before they become problems; helps others think about how to define or redefine complex problems. Supports business leaders to find solutions and evaluates others’ solutions to determine the best way forward. Understand how to resolve escalated issues and coaches others to problem solve. Manages escalations.

Stakeholder Management – Advanced - Capitalizes on deep understanding of (current or potential) client and agency organizational structures, business processes, strategic objectives and challenges in order to anticipate and meet their needs. Demonstrates expert knowledge and monitors the client’s industry and competitive environment in order to create effective solutions. Advises key stakeholders by continuously helping them to successfully navigate through critical business changes.​​​​​​​ Uses strong deep expertise and contextual awareness to explore complex issues with stakeholders and provide trusted advice, deliverables and campaign KPIs.

Effective Communication – Advanced - Leads the delivery of relevant and accurate information to drive maximum impact. Consistently delivers communications to influence and educate all levels of seniority, appropriately judging the demands of the situation. Creatively develops presentations and comms to help with the understanding/education of complex information. Guides others on the best practices and approaches for creating clear, concise and organized communication materials to convey plans in a user-friendly way.

Campaign Management – Expert - Sets the standard for accuracy and thoroughness so that sufficiently detailed information is logged correctly.  Balances short-term considerations with long-term goals and ensures that critical deliverables are met.  Manages multiple overlapping timelines and competing demands, weighing the needs of different stakeholders across the business to determine priorities for parallel projects and sets priorities according to business needs.

Compelling storytelling – Advanced - Lead and direct the creation of a story, taking into account client knowledge levels and needs. Applies deep expertise and sound judgement to persuade key decision makers on recommendation, considering all implications. Designs differentiated communications (content focus, style, presentation, etc.) for various internal and external audiences.

Ideas Creation – Expert - Develops strategies to bring new technologies, innovations and products to life.  Challenges the client and team in innovating and designing new solutions, methods and products to remain competitive and lead the industry.

Comms Planning – Advanced - High technical knowledge of all media touchpoints as well as how they interplay and future trends.  Serves as a consultant and quality controls plans, strategies and frameworks that leave the building.  Strategic learnings and insights about business impact (not just media metrics).  Development of directional media strategy/platform.  Developing comms planning skills amongst wider community.  Looks for alternative solutions to problems and constantly challenges received norms in a spirit of positive provocation.

Our passion for shaping the next era of media is powered by our commitment to Be Extraordinary, investing in our employees to inspire transformational creativity. We also Lead Optimistically, firmly believing in and Championing Growth and Development for every individual. This commitment allows WPP Media employees to leverage the extensive global WPP Media & WPP networks to pursue their passions, build vital professional connections, and learn at the cutting edge of marketing and advertising.  

We Create an Open environment built on trust and respect, where everyone feels they belong and has opportunities to progress. Our comprehensive benefits package reflects this commitment, including competitive medical, group retirement plans, vision, and dental insurance, significant paid time off, preferential partner discounts, and employee mental health awareness days.  

WPP Media is an equal opportunity employer and considers applicants for all positions without discrimination or regard to characteristics. If you require accommodations or flexibility, please discuss this with the hiring team during the interview process.  Please note that while our philosophy is the same across WPP, benefits may vary by office/country.

title: Director, Sales Engineering - Europe
descriptionHtml:
About CoreView   

CoreView is the global leader in Microsoft 365 (M365) tenant resilience, serving over 23 million users worldwide. We empower the world’s leading organizations to master the complexity of Microsoft M365.  Through robust security and precise governance, we help ensure that our client’s environments stay cyber-resilient and productive, no matter how complex they are.  
 
Our unified, cloud-native platform delivers powerful automation, rapid value, and end-to-end visibility across the entire M365 ecosystem. Backed by world-class support and a collaborative, innovative culture, CoreView is a place where your ideas matter, and your work truly impacts global enterprises.  

(Candidate must be located in and have the right to work in the United Kingdom)

Job Summary:

CoreView is seeking a Director of Sales Engineering to lead our Sales Engineering function across EMEA. Based in the UK and reporting to the Global VP of Sales Engineering, this is a player-coach role: you will lead, develop, and scale a high-performing team of Sales Engineers while personally running technical strategy on our most strategic and complex opportunities. 

You will be the senior technical voice for CoreView in the region – partnering with Sales, Partner, Customer Success, and Product leadership to drive new business and expansion revenue, raise the bar on technical sales execution, and help customers strengthen Microsoft 365 security, improve administrative control, reduce operational burden, and build tenant resilience. This is a key leadership role with a direct impact on regional growth, team capability, and how CoreView wins. 

Responsibilities: 

Leadership & Team Development 

  • Lead, coach, and develop the EMEA Sales Engineering team, setting clear expectations for discovery, demonstration, proof-of-value, and technical win execution
  • Recruit, hire, and onboard top Sales Engineering talent as the region scales
  • Drive individual development plans and contribute to the global SE career framework, skills matrix, and progression routes
  • Run regular deal reviews, demo and discovery coaching, and certification to build consistent, repeatable technical sales excellence
  • Own SE resource allocation and capacity planning across EMEA opportunities, balancing coverage across new business, expansion, partner, and public sector motions
  • Foster a collaborative, high-accountability culture that is aligned with the global Sales Engineering organization 

Strategic Opportunity Leadership 

  • Personally lead the technical sales strategy on a portfolio of the largest and most strategic EMEA opportunities, working alongside senior Account Executives and Sales leadership
  • Engage C-level and senior IT, security, and operations stakeholders to articulate CoreView’s business value and differentiated position
  • Lead executive-level discovery, solution design, and compelling technical presentations and product demonstrations aligned to customer priorities such as:
  • Secure Microsoft 365 administration at scale
  • Delegated administration across business units, regions, departments, or agencies
  • Configuration backup and recovery for tenant resilience
  • Policy enforcement and drift detection
  • Workflow automation
  • Hybrid and multi-tenant visibility and management
  • Design and run proof-of-value programs for strategic opportunities, with clear success criteria tied to business outcomes
  • Act as the technical escalation point for complex, high-value, or at-risk deals across the region
  • Lead technical responses to strategic RFPs/RFIs and public sector tenders 

Regional Strategy & Cross-Functional Partnership 

  • Partner with EMEA Sales leadership on territory and account strategy, pipeline generation, and forecasting
  • Own technical win forecasting and pipeline hygiene for the EMEA SE team, ensuring accurate and timely updates in Salesforce
  • Work closely with Product Management and Engineering to represent EMEA customer requirements, competitive insight, and regional needs (including data residency, GDPR, and public sector requirements)
  • Collaborate with Partner and Alliance teams to enable Microsoft resellers, system integrators, and managed service providers across the region
  • Partner with Customer Success and Professional Services to ensure smooth technical handover and long-term customer value
  • Represent CoreView as a thought leader at customer briefings, webinars, conferences, and Microsoft and partner events 

Operational Excellence 

  • Define, track, and report on SE team KPIs such as technical win rate, proof-of-value conversion, SE coverage, and pipeline contribution
  • Drive adoption of consistent SE processes, tooling, and methodology (including MEDDICC/MEDDPICC) across the region
  • Contribute to and maintain demo environments, technical sales assets, competitive materials, and reference architectures
  • Ensure alignment with CoreView’s Information Security Management System and contribute to the Information Security Program 

Requirements: 

  • Minimum of 10 years’ experience in pre-sales technical roles (Sales Engineer, Solutions Architect, or similar) within enterprise SaaS
  • Minimum of 3 years’ experience leading and developing Sales Engineering or pre-sales teams, ideally across multiple EMEA countries
  • Proven track record of personally leading technical strategy on large, complex enterprise deals with multiple senior stakeholders
  • Expert knowledge of Microsoft 365, Entra ID (Azure AD), and hybrid environments (including on-premise Active Directory)
  • Strong technical proficiency across Microsoft 365 administration, Exchange, security and compliance, and Microsoft cloud technologies
  • Exceptional executive presence, with the ability to convey complex technical solutions to C-level and non-technical stakeholders
  • Experience hiring, coaching, and building high-performing teams, with a demonstrable approach to skills development and career progression
  • Data-driven approach to team performance, forecasting, and capacity planning
  • Strong commercial acumen and experience working closely with Sales leadership on forecasting and deal strategy
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Ability to work collaboratively across a global, distributed organization and multiple time zones
  • Based in the UK with the right to work in the UK
  • Ability to travel across the UK and EMEA, with occasional travel to the US (up to 40%)
  • Familiarity with MEDDICC/MEDDPICC sales methodology
  • Experience working with Microsoft partners, resellers, and the Microsoft field is an advantage
  • Experience selling into UK public sector, government, or regulated industries is an advantage
  • Eligibility and willingness to obtain UK Security Check (SC) clearance is an advantage
  • Experience with PowerShell scripting and automation workflows is an advantage
  • Additional European language skills are an advantage

Ownership Mindset:Take ownership. Drive outcomes. 

One Team: One team, one goal, embracing diversity - to achieve more together. 

Velocity: Decide fast. Deliver fast. Repeat.

Continuous Improvement: Curiosity drives us. We challenge the status quo.

Customer First: Listen deeply. Solve boldly.
