  • Have a background in, or real curiosity about, pharma, biotech, healthcare or AI

  • Like working in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment where collaboration across teams is the norm

  • Are ready to learn quickly and bring your own ideas

What happens next:
If your profile aligns with a current or future need, we will contact you to arrange a conversation. Otherwise, with your consent, we will keep your details on file and reach out when a suitable opportunity arises.

What we offer

  • Flexible work organization

  • Friendly and informal working environment

  • Opportunity to work with an international team with high technical and scientific backgrounds

Recruitment Process & Security

  • Please complete the form and submit your CV.

  • Owkin is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, sex, gender, sexual orientation, age, color, religion, national origin, protected veteran status or on the basis of disability.

  • Owkin is a great place to work. As a coveted workplace we are, unfortunately, vulnerable to recruitment phishing scams. We urge all job seekers and candidates to be wary of potential scams. Most of these have individuals posing as representatives of prominent companies, including Owkin, with the aim of obtaining personal, sensitive, or financial information from applicants. These scams prey upon an individual’s desire to obtain a job and can sometimes “feel” like a genuine recruitment process. Some red flags are identified below. Should you encounter a recruitment process that claims to be for Owkin but is not consistent with the below, please do not provide any personal or financial information:

  • Legitimate Owkin recruitment processes include communication with candidates through recognized professional networks, such as LinkedIn.

  • Communication is always through an official Owkin email address (from the @owkin.com domain), over the phone or through our applicant tracking system (Ashby).

  • The Owkin talent team do use platforms such as LinkedIn, however if you have any concern or doubt about this contact, please ask for them to send an email from @Owkin.com.

  • The Owkin talent team will not solicit personal data from candidates during the application phase including, but not limited to, date of birth, social security numbers, or bank account information;

  • Legitimate Owkin interviews may be conducted over the phone, in person, or via an approved enterprise videoconferencing service (Google Meets). They will not occur via Signal, Telegram or Messenger

  • Owkin offers of employment are based on merit and only extended once a candidate has interviewed with members of the talent and hiring team. Offers will be extended both verbally and in written format.

If you think that you have been a victim of fraud,

  • Check the identity of the talent team on LinkedIn

  • Check our senior team on our website https://owkin.com/team/

  • Check the existence of the position on our website: https://www.owkin.com/careers#current-opportunities

  • Notify Owkin's recruitment unit at this address contact the following authorities:

    • [FR] https://internet-signalement.gouv.fr/

    • [UK] https://www.actionfraud.police.uk/reporting-fraud-and-cyber-crime

    • [US] https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/

title: Sr. Medical Director, Germany
descriptionHtml:
About Acadia Pharmaceuticals   Acadia is committed to turning scientific promise into meaningful innovation that makes the difference for underserved neurological and rare disease communities around the world. Our commercial portfolio includes the first and only FDA-approved treatments for Parkinson’s disease psychosis and Rett syndrome. We are developing the next wave of therapeutic advancements with a robust and diverse pipeline that includes mid- to late-stage programs in Alzheimer’s disease psychosis and Lewy body dementia psychosis, along with earlier-stage programs that address other underserved patient needs. At Acadia, we’re here to be their difference.

Position Summary

The Sr. Medical Director, Germany will lead the development and execution of the local medical affairs strategy together with the field Medical Science Liaisons (MSLs) and in line with the European Medical Affairs strategy and the local country strategy for RETT syndrome including the integrated medical plans with full medical budget ownership and responsibility. Responsibilities will include building and maintaining external stakeholder relationships and collaborations, as well as continuing to position Acadia as a thought leader and valued partner with patient advocacy groups (PAG) and medical/scientific RETT community in Germany. This individual will be responsible for the effectiveness and compliance of scientific exchange conducted to meet the needs of clinicians, patient advocates, and other key external and internal stakeholders.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Provide scientific and medical leadership, including development of strategic country medical affairs (post-launch) plans, identifying specific unmet medical needs, and data gaps.
  • Leading the local medical affairs team.
  • Ensure strong medical/scientific leadership in coordination and participation in country MRC/MLR procedures.
  • Establish appropriate strategic partnerships with Centers of Excellence, KOLs, and PAGs, in areas of scientific interest.
  • Ensure aligned and close cross-functional collaboration, with country GM, Market Access, other relevant country and international staff to optimally manage relationships and ensure alignment and effective execution of the German medical strategy.
  • Coordinate and ensure operational medical excellence, in collaboration with EU medical teams and aligned with country strategy, to capture and track key medical tactics and medical (post-launch) activities in Germany.
  • Provide medical expertise and editorial support in data dissemination at conferences and in medical journals, as appropriate.
  • Involvement with key HCPs in the exchange of scientific and medical information including Advisory Boards and presentations at national meetings and conferences.
  • Develop and maintain, together with MSLs, close professional relationships with KOLs and emerging scientific leaders in the community.
  • Oversee gathering and reporting field medical insights through existing Veeva CRM system and in line with company rules and requirements.
  • Oversee and communicate to cross-functional stakeholders the insights the MSL team gains about competitive landscape, unmet needs of physicians and advocacy groups. Develops potential actionable plans to address these local insights.
  • Manages publication activities, including review and approval of abstracts and manuscripts, local publication strategy and real-world evidence development and compliant collaboration with authors, as needed.

Education/Experience/Skills

  • MD highly preferred; PhD, PharmD, or an equivalent qualification may also be considered.
  • 15+ years of Medical Affairs leadership experience in the biopharmaceutical industry in Germany or the DACH region; broader regional experience is advantageous.
  • Prior team-management experience is required.
  • Substantial rare-disease—preferably neurological—experience in Germany and/or the DACH region.
  • Extensive knowledge of the German healthcare system and applicable national rules and regulations.
  • Significant experience coordinating and participating in national MLR/MRC procedures.
  • Experience engaging with rare-disease patient advocacy groups is highly preferred.

Key Skills

  • Extensive knowledge to critically appraise studies and clinical evidence to allow engagement on higher scientific level with HCPs.
  • In depth understanding of compliance and regulatory requirements, including extensive personal experience and expertise with MRC/MLR procedures, for pharmaceutical Medical Affairs, R&D and Commercial activities in Germany.
  • Excellent communication, collaboration, and presentation skills, and experience in the delivery of scientific presentations.
  • Agile, independent and proactive working style.
  • Personal sense of purpose, confidence, and stand fest in challenging situations.
  • Ability to build strong cross-functional and cross-company relationships.
  • Ability to collaborate and share information to contribute to the planning process and execute the agreed local Medical (pre)launch plan, together with MSL team, and in line with Regional Medical Affairs strategy.
  • Fluency in German at native or near-native level and strong English proficiency are required, with the ability to communicate complex details clearly.
  • Ability to travel both locally and internationally is required.

At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

About Axon

Axon's mission is simple and bold: Protect Life.

We build technology that helps first responders, security teams and communities act with speed, clarity and confidence in the moments that matter most. Our Real-Time Operations (RTO) portfolio, anchored by the Fusus platform, is transforming how law enforcement, enterprise security and international agencies detect, assess and respond to threats.

Fusus connects live video, alerts, sensors and location data into a unified operating picture. Mobile is where that picture meets the field. It's the phone in an officer's pocket, the screen in a patrol car, the device a security lead carries across a campus. We're building fast, dependable mobile experiences that put the right information in responders' hands wherever they are.

Your Impact

As Senior Product Manager for Fusus Mobile, you will define and lead the strategy and roadmap for how Fusus works on the move. Your goal is to make mobile a first-class surface of real-time operations, not a smaller copy of the web.

You'll own the Fusus mobile platform and its primary apps: the experiences officers, supervisors and security teams use to receive alerts, view livestreams, see who is nearby and coordinate response. You'll also own the foundations other Axon teams build on, so new capabilities reach mobile at the same time as web.

You'll lead our boldest bets on mobile: personalised, role-based experiences that adapt to each user, AI-assisted workflows in the field, and new form factors such as in-vehicle (CarPlay and Android Auto), tablets and wearables. Your work will help responders around the world act faster and stay safer, and directly advance Axon's mission to Protect Life.

Work Location: This role is based out of our London office and follows a hybrid schedule. We rely on in-person collaboration and ask that team members work onsite Tuesdays through Fridays, with the flexibility to work remotely on Mondays, unless there is an approved workplace accommodation. We believe that connection fuels innovation, and our in-office culture is designed to foster meaningful teamwork, mentorship, and shared success.

What You'll Do

  • Own the Fusus Mobile product strategy and roadmap across iOS and Android
  • Define the mobile platform (shared components, navigation, notifications, identity) that lets other teams ship features on mobile alongside web
  • Lead personalised and role-based mobile experiences, using mobile as the proving ground before they move to web
  • Close the gap between mobile and web for core workflows such as alerts, livestreaming, maps and search
  • Make the apps dependable in the field: offline behaviour, poor connectivity, battery, background location and push
  • Partner with engineering (UK, U.S. and Romania) and design to plan, release and monitor mobile versions on a predictable cadence
  • Engage law enforcement and enterprise users in the field (ride-alongs, site visits, betas) to validate needs and test improvements
  • Use metrics and feedback to set priorities: daily active use, crash-free sessions, time from alert to action, app store ratings
  • Support go-to-market, training, enablement and rollout with Customer Success, Professional Services and Sales

What Success Looks Like

  • Responders reach for Fusus Mobile first because it is fast, reliable and built for how they work in the field
  • New Fusus capabilities launch on mobile at the same time as web
  • Personalised experiences help each user see what matters to their role, with less setup and less noise
  • Adoption grows across customer segments with high daily use, strong retention and positive field feedback

What You Bring

  • 7–10 years of product management experience, including 3+ years owning native mobile products (iOS and Android)
  • Experience building products where speed, clarity and reliability directly affect outcomes
  • Strong grasp of mobile platform concepts: release management and app stores, push notifications, background location, offline sync, device and OS fragmentation
  • Familiarity with real-time data, live video, maps and geolocation, alerting, or IoT integrations
  • Track record of turning field and user insight into clear product direction and focused execution
  • Proven ability to lead cross-functional and distributed teams through roadmap, design, delivery and iteration
  • Clear communicator who drives alignment, decisions and measurable outcomes

Nice to have

  • Experience in public safety, security, logistics, field service or other mission-critical domains
  • Experience with personalisation, in-vehicle (CarPlay / Android Auto) or wearable experiences, or AI-assisted mobile workflows
  • Experience building a mobile platform or SDK used by other product teams

Why Axon

Benefits that Benefit You

title: Staff Economist, Marketplace Economics
descriptionHtml:
Change the way the world travels

Join the GetYourGuide journey to connect people with unforgettable travel experiences around the world. Millions look to us for unique activities they can trust, and it’s all powered by our commitment to make every single journey extraordinary - including yours.

Ready to unlock your potential with a community of fellow explorers? Find your next role at our Berlin HQ or one of our local offices around the globe, from New York to Bangkok. Head to getyourguide.careers to take the first step.

Team mission

Marketplace Economics is a new team at GetYourGuide, built to answer the questions that determine how our marketplace grows and how it should be designed. How much revenue does the next euro of paid search actually return? Which marketing channels are genuinely incremental, and which are taking credit for demand we already had? What price should a supplier set, what does a change in commission do to supply, demand, and liquidity, and how should our ranking and supplier incentives be structured in the first place?

We are a senior team working directly with leadership across Marketing, Pricing, and Supply, among others, and the decisions we inform are among the largest the company makes. On the causal inference side, we draw on tools like experimental design, natural and quasi-experiments, double machine learning, synthetic controls, and more to inform marketing attribution and incrementality, spend allocation, and price elasticity. Our structural work models demand, supply, and the mechanisms connecting them, so we can reason about equilibrium outcomes and simulate counterfactuals we can't run as experiments. Most of our hardest problems in pricing and market design need both.

Your mission

You'll be a technical lead for pricing and supply and a core contributor to our marketplace measurement work. Reporting to the Director of Marketplace Economics, you will:

  • Own the economics of pricing end to end: estimate travel demand and willingness to pay, build the structural models that turn those estimates into defensible price recommendations for our supply partners, and run the experiments that validate them.

  • Work collaboratively with other economists on paid marketing optimization problems across channels and geographies and funnel stages.

  • Work on the design of the marketplace itself; commission and incentive structures, inventory coverage, supply liquidity.

  • Partner closely with business leads in Marketing, Pricing, and Supply by translating ambiguous commercial questions into reasonable identification strategies that drive meaningful business outcomes.

  • Set the technical bar for empirical rigor at GetYourGuide: raise the quality of experiment design across teams, mentor analysts and data scientists.

Your toolkit

  • PhD in Economics, or a closely related quantitative discipline with a strong applied focus.

  • 5+ years of applied work after your PhD, including 2+ years at a marketplace or platform company.

  • Comfort with structural work: discrete choice and demand estimation, equilibrium and counterfactual simulation, and the industrial organization or market design toolkit for reasoning about mechanisms, incentives, and two-sided platform dynamics.

  • Expertise in causal inference: experimental design, difference-in-differences, synthetic control, regression discontinuity, double/debiased ML, and Bayesian approaches to media measurement.

  • The judgment to choose between these approaches for the problem in front of you, and to say clearly what each one can and cannot support.

  • Strong Python and SQL, and comfort working with production-scale data alongside data engineers and scientists.

  • A track record of your analysis influencing business decisions.

  • Genuine enthusiasm for stakeholder work: excellent written and spoken English, and the judgment to know when a simpler answer is the right one.

Extras that give you an edge

  • Pricing, demand estimation, or revenue management experience in a two-sided marketplace.

  • Market or mechanism design work in production: matching, ranking, allocation, or incentive systems that real users transacted through.

  • Experience working alongside ML and data science teams and shipping methods into production systems.

How we’ll make your career journey extraordinary

  • Annual personal growth budget and mentorship programs for continuous learning and development

  • Become a part of our success with virtual share options

  • Work from anywhere in the world for 30 days per year

  • A hybrid working approach with three days of in-office collaboration (Mon, Tue, Thur) and two days of optional at-home focus time. 

  • Opportunities to collaborate and socialize  with a quarterly team event budget 

  • Access to leading AI tools plus the resources and budget to get the most out of them

  • Monthly transportation and fitness budget

  • Discounts for you, your friends, and family on GetYourGuide activities

  • Language reimbursement program

  • Health and wellness benefits

And more…

title: Staff Engineer - Fintech
descriptionHtml:
Help make the world more hospitable

The hospitality industry is uniquely human, and it deserves technology that’s just as inspiring as the people behind it. At Mews, we’re transforming the industry with a platform that helps hotels run smarter, move faster and create better guest experiences.

You’ll work with smart, curious people who care deeply about what they do. You’ll have autonomy and the trust to make good decisions and move quickly. And you’ll enjoy a real sense of purpose as you see the impact of what we’re building.

If you’re motivated by ownership, curiosity and meaningful impact, and are driven to deliver consistent high performance, you’ll feel at home here.

About the role

Let's get into the specifics. It’s impossible to capture every nuance of a role – especially at a rapidly growing company like Mews – but if we had to distil it into a job description (which we do because this is a job description), it would be this:

You will own the agents, skills and standards that let a tribe of product builders move quickly on payments without the architecture fragmenting. Hotels take payments across regions and through providers that each behave differently, and Payment Interfaces exists to give customers one coherent payment experience on top of several PSPs. Embedded payments at this depth is rare among European SaaS companies, so the problems here are ones few engineers get to work on.

You will be a Staff Engineer in the Payment Interfaces team, part of the Fintech tribe. You will report to the Director of Product and Engineering, sit in the tribe’s leadership group, and work alongside product builders, other staff engineers and product managers. No one reports to you, so your influence comes from the architecture, tools and standards that other people choose to work in.

The team integrates several PSPs depending on region and conditions. When integrations drift apart, builders slow down and quality suffers. This role exists to keep them coherent by encoding what good looks like into tools and agents, so every builder meets the standard by default.

What you would do 

  • Own the tribe’s engineering agents, skills and context, and encode architectural standards, review logic and quality gates into them so the standard is met by default.
  • Build an AI first responder for customer tickets about payment issues, with clear rules for when it answers and when it hands over to a person.
  • Stay hands-on for the hardest technical problems: migrations, system-wide refactors and long-lived architecture decisions across PSP integrations.
  • Keep Payment Interfaces integrations coherent as PSPs and regional requirements change, collaborating with builders who own their own work.
  • Coach builders and fix off-standard outcomes at the cause, so the lesson sticks.

AI Fluency Level 4: in this role, that means you build the AI systems the tribe works in, not only use them. You design the agents, skills and evaluations that builders rely on every day, make the engineering decisions about how they behave, and set the rules for when an AI answer can stand and when a person must step in.

For more information on AI fluency at Mews, please refer to “AI Fluency at Mews: A Comprehensive Guide for Candidates” on Confluence.

What you would bring 

  • Hands-on experience integrating with payment service providers or payment processors.
  • Deep engineering craft and architectural judgment, including a sense of what is worth codifying and what is a one-off.
  • AI Fluency Level 4 or the equivalent hands-on experience: you have built agents, skills, evaluations or tooling that other engineers use, and you can explain where human oversight stays non-negotiable.
  • A systems mindset that turns hard-won knowledge into reusable architecture and tooling rather than documentation.
  • Comfort with influence as your main way of getting things done, working with builders, product managers, principals and senior leaders without anyone reporting to you.

Nice to have 

  • Experience in hospitality, travel or another operationally complex B2B SaaS environment.
  • Experience publishing or speaking externally about your work.
  • A track record of coaching other engineers and multiplying their effectiveness.

What’s in it for you?

Our success is powered by our incredible people, supported by benefits that help them thrive.

Global benefits

No matter where you’re based, you’ll enjoy:

  • Unlimited paid holiday (yes, really)
  • Participation in our company share program
  • Paid parental leave (6 months fully paid for primary caregivers, 2 months for secondary, available after one year of service)

Local benefits

You'll receive additional benefits that vary by location, from healthcare and retirement plans to team events, socials and other perks. Ask us about it during your interview process.

Life at Mews

We’re an equal opportunities employer. We value teams that reflect the diversity of the customers and communities we serve. Different perspectives make better ideas, stronger products and a more welcoming company.

We also believe transparency is important when deciding if you're the right fit. Mews is an ambitious, high-pressure environment of continuous learning and high standards. Success here requires resilience, adaptability and a willingness to solve difficult problems.

A few things that define how we work:

  • High autonomy means high responsibility. People are expected to take ownership and drive outcomes. There isn’t a detailed playbook for everything, and that’s part of what makes the work challenging – and rewarding.
  • Change is constant. We’re growing quickly and adapting as we scale. Teams, processes and priorities continue to evolve, and only people who stay curious and agile will thrive.

  • AI is an integral part of our processes. It’s not here to steal people’s jobs, but to amplify efficiency and productivity. We’re motivated to proactively use the technology to seek out better ways of working and share our findings with the rest of the company.

If there's anything we can do to support you during the application process, let us know.

We don't discriminate on the basis of race, religion, colour, nationality, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other protected characteristic.

One final thing: don't hold back. If you don't meet 100% of the criteria in this job description but you're certain you could make a big impact, apply. Everyone should have equal access to opportunities, and we're committed to providing an inclusive experience.

If Mews sounds like the kind of environment where you'd thrive, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Staff Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Staff Engineer

You'll be the most senior engineer on the agents that run finance operations for our customers — designing, building, and operating the autonomous agents that handle accounts payable and receivable end-to-end. From invoice validation and dispute resolution to cross-company negotiation and cash optimization.

This is an individual-contributor role at the top of our ladder: no direct reports, full technical authority over the architecture the rest of the team builds on.

What you'll do

  • Agent architecture — Design the multi-agent system: agent boundaries, event contracts, orchestration patterns, and the separation between LLM reasoning and deterministic enforcement. LLMs inform; rules enforce. You own where that line sits for every action that moves money, and the authorization gateway that makes it non-negotiable.

  • Agentic dispute resolution — An agent that reads the claim, gathers the evidence from the PO, contract, and delivery record, forms a position, and works it to settlement — negotiating with the counterparty where that's appropriate, escalating to a human where it isn't. Deductions and short pays classified, tied to the underlying claim, and driven to resolution rather than parked in an aging bucket.

  • Agentic dynamic discounting — Agents that continuously price early payment against the cash position on both sides of the transaction, propose terms, and execute them. Static payment terms become a negotiation that runs on its own.

  • Matching and reconciliation — Three-way matching across purchase order, goods receipt, and invoice with configurable tolerances; cash application against bank statements and remittance advices, including partial payments and residuals; the exception paths that follow when any of it fails. Unglamorous but important: The foundation everything agentic sits on.

  • Validation & anomaly detection — Business rule checks, duplicate and near-duplicate detection, pricing discrepancy detection, and anomaly detection across time. Precision matters as much as recall here: a false positive is a blocked supplier and an angry procurement lead.

  • Integration framework — ERP systems first and deepest, then banking APIs, accounting platforms, Gmail, Drive, and Slack. Auth model, credential lifecycle, data normalization. Today each connector is a project; you make the next one a configuration.

  • Compliance & security — Agents operate within a zero-trust model. You'll design how agents verify independently against source data, how outbound content is reviewed, and how the system prevents cascading failures from prompt injection. Plus the European e-invoicing mandates now landing across France, Germany, and Spain, and what EN 16931 means for the pipeline.

  • Platform & data infrastructure — Own the primitives every agent action rests on: an append-only PostgreSQL event store with tamper-evident hash chaining for replay and audit; cryptographic signature verification on agent events and approval chains before anything external fires; the Workflow Constraint Engine that gates payments, emails, and API calls on deterministic policy, not model output; row-level multi-tenancy and tenant-scoped credentials across every data store; attribute-based authorization via Cerbos, evaluated the same way whether the caller is an agent or a human; and the MCP security layer — auth, capability-scoping, rate limiting — for external agent-to-agent access.

  • The engineering standard — Architecture decision records, review bar, on-call, and a clear view of what we deliberately don't build. You'll write the things the next ten engineers read in week one, and you'll spend time with controllers and AP leads watching agents fail in ways no test predicted.

What we're looking for

  • 8+ years shipping production systems; currently Staff, Principal, Lead IC, or a founding engineer. You've carried an architecture through a scaling step and lived with your own decisions.

  • Strong systems design thinking — agent boundaries, failure modes, trust boundaries, contract evolution. Money movement is not retry-safe by default and you already know why.

  • Depth in Python and/or TypeScript in production, and deep PostgreSQL: event sourcing, row-level security, indexing tradeoffs, schema evolution under load.

  • Hands-on experience with LLM-powered systems, agent orchestration frameworks (LangGraph, LangChain, or similar), and document AI (LlamaIndex, LlamaParse, or similar).

  • Strong opinions about when to use an LLM vs. a rules engine vs. traditional ML — and the courage to defend them.

  • Experience designing data pipelines, integration architectures, or event-driven systems in production.

  • Security awareness — you think about what happens when untrusted input meets your pipeline, and about segregation of duties before someone makes you.

  • Technical leadership without a title: reviews that teach, designs that get adopted, engineers who get faster because you're there.

  • Effective use of AI coding tools with strong review skills for LLM integration and auth code.

  • Domain knowledge across the purchase-to-pay and order-to-cash cycle. You don't need all three areas below, but you need real depth in one and working fluency in the rest — enough that when a controller describes an exception, you understand it before they finish:

    • Accounts payable — PO and non-PO invoice intake, coding to GL account and cost centre, approval routing and delegation of authority, three-way matching and tolerance handling, blocked-invoice and exception workflows, duplicate detection, payment runs, payment terms and early-payment discounts, supplier master data and bank-detail verification, period-end accruals for un-invoiced receipts.

    • Accounts receivable — invoice issuance and e-invoicing, cash application and remittance matching, partial payments, short pays and residuals, credit memos, deductions and dispute handling, dunning and collections strategy, credit limits and credit risk, aging and DSO.

    • Procurement — requisition to purchase order, supplier onboarding and qualification, catalogues and contract pricing, goods receipt, off-contract and maverick spend, sourcing and supplier negotiation, and the handoff into AP where most of the pain actually lives.

  • Fluency with the systems this runs on: ERPs (NetSuite, Dynamics, or the SMB stack), the sub-ledger to general-ledger relationship, and how period close constrains what an agent is allowed to do and when.

Nice to have:

  • Peppol and EN 16931 in production, or bank connectivity via ISO 20022.

  • Cryptographic primitives in production: digital signatures, hash chaining, tamper-evident logs.

  • SOC 2, GDPR, or data-residency engineering in a regulated environment.

  • You've founded something, or have been employee 1 to 5 in a startup.

title: Staff Product Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About Parloa

Parloa's mission is to make every customer conversation feel effortless for both customers and the companies serving them. As agentic AI accelerates, Parloans are shaping the foundation of a new era in customer experience, one where customer support is no longer transactions, but meaningful exchanges. It is not just a vision; Parloa has powered over ONE BILLION interactions between global enterprise brands and their customers, with companies like Booking.com, HealthEquity, Allianz, SAP, BarmeniaGothaer, and TUI already deploying Parloa at scale.

About the role:

As a Staff Product Engineer, you will work directly inside our most strategic enterprise customers. You will build the software that makes their AI agents work in production, and be measured by the difference it makes for the customer.

Our agents are built by business users in Parloa’s platform, AMP. AMP already comes with a broad library of tools and integrations. Your job is the part AMP does not cover yet for a given customer: the last connection into their systems, or a capability the product does not have. Our customers are large enterprises in financial services, telecom, insurance, travel and retail. For them, a working prototype is where an engagement starts, not where it ends.

The work comes in two forms. Some engagements run for years. You stay with the account, deepen its integrations and help it grow into new use cases. Others are short experiments. You test a new idea with a real customer and decide quickly whether it is worth building. At Staff level, you take on the hardest cases of both: accounts where a pilot-grade solution would fail in production, and capabilities nobody at Parloa has built before. Staff means harder problems and more ambiguity, not less hands-on work.

On many accounts, you work alongside a Deployment Strategist. Think of the two of you as the account’s leadership team. The Deployment Strategist acts as its CPO and defines what success looks like. You act as its CTO and own the architecture and the build. On accounts without a Deployment Strategist, you own the engineering yourself.

Areas of ownership:

  • Lead the hardest engagements. Run complex programmes with several workstreams. Make the architecture decisions that span Parloa’s platform and several parts of the customer’s organization.

  • Build what AMP does not cover yet. Systems of record, telephony and contact-center integrations, state management, data readiness, multi-agent orchestration and retrieval. When the answer is unclear, build a prototype quickly and decide whether it is worth pursuing before Parloa invests a full quarter in it.

  • Own production quality and security. Evals, production readiness, observability and incident playbooks for enterprise-scale traffic. Meet the data handling standards a regulated customer expects, including PII, access control and audit trails. Debug live issues, whether they are technical or caused by model behaviour.

  • Grow the account, and share what belongs in the product. Drive the second use case, the second business unit, the renewal. Set the delivery standard for other engineers on complex accounts. When something you build would help every customer, flag it. That is how Parloa decides what goes into the core product.

  • Mentor other Product Engineers, and take part in interviewing and hiring.

  • Use AI well, and set the standard for it. Decide how AI-assisted work is validated before it reaches a customer’s production traffic.

  • Represent Parloa with senior technical stakeholders. Work directly with the customer’s principal engineers, architects and security leaders. Be the engineer commercial teams bring in when a prospect asks how the solution would work for them.

What this role is not:

  • Not running the Parloa platform itself. That is a separate engineering role. The platform is your foundation, and you build what a specific customer needs on top of it.

  • Not agent configuration. Business users design and configure agents in AMP. You build the integrations and capabilities those agents need.

  • Not a people-management role. You are an individual contributor and write and review code every week.

OUR TECH STACK:

Go, TypeScript, Node.js, Python, FastAPI, frontier LLMs, MCP, Azure, Kubernetes, Docker, Terraform, MongoDB, Redis, Kafka/NATS

You will not use all of these, and most engagements add something new.

Who you are:

  • 5+ years leading the design and architecture of large-scale production systems in customer-facing or enterprise environments, with a focus on reliability, scale and failure modes.

  • Experience leading agentic, spec-driven development in production. You know when a coding agent’s output is wrong and what checks it needs before it ships.

  • A track record in long-term accounts or fast experiments. You have owned a strategic enterprise relationship over several years, through an expansion, a renewal or a leadership change. Or you have tested new ideas at the frontier and decided quickly whether they were worth building.

  • Experience as a mentor or tech lead, helping engineers become independent.

  • Comfortable with ambiguity and with customers. You work well in complex organizations, build trust quickly with new customer teams, spot risks early and keep your judgment when the stakes are high.

  • Willingness to travel up to 25% to customer sites, depending on the engagement.

  • Strong spoken and written communication skills in English.

Nice to have:

  • Experience building or deploying an LLM-powered system used by real users in production

  • Hands-on experience with eval frameworks, agent tooling, RAG, prompt engineering or multi-agent orchestration (few candidates will have all of these)

  • A founder or founding-engineer background

  • Forward-deployed, solutions engineering, product engineering or strategic-partner experience at an enterprise software or AI company

  • Voice or conversational AI, or contact center, telephony or CCaaS integration

  • Experience in regulated industries such as banking, insurance or telecom

Our engineering values:

At Parloa, we hire, promote, and evaluate based on cultural and technical excellence. You’ll thrive here if you:

  • Earn Trust – act with transparency and reliability.

  • Obsess Over Customers – always start with the customer problem.

  • Think Big – set bold goals and pursue them fearlessly.

Why Parloa?

We're at the beginning of a new era in customer experience, one where AI doesn't just respond, but understands, reasons, and takes action. When millions of people reach out to a brand, those interactions aren't just support tickets; they're defining experiences. We're here to raise the standard: making every conversation seamless, intelligent, and genuinely helpful. title: Staff Robot Control Software Engineer (f/m/d)
descriptionHtml:
Your tasks

Imagine fleets of autonomous forklifts, each weighing several tons, lifting heavy loads into racks up to 14 meters high, safely and around the clock, right next to people. That's what we build at Jungheinrich Robotics, and AI-assisted engineering plays an important role in how we do it. In this role, you ensure that every one of these vehicles moves exactly as intended.

We are hiring at both Senior and Staff levels. Apply for the role that fits you best, and we'll find the right fit together!

  • You take ownership of the control software for our autonomous forklifts, from a unified hardware abstraction layer and actuator control based on ros_control/ros2_control to the interfaces with localization and navigation.
  • You model and implement vehicle kinematics for different forklift types, including acceleration- and jerk-limited motion.
  • You integrate motor controllers, drives, and actuators using fieldbus systems, particularly CANopen.
  • You integrate and calibrate robot sensors, including encoders, IMUs, laser scanners, cameras, and lift height sensors.
  • You improve the reliability of our robots in real-world environments through intelligent error handling, automated recovery mechanisms, and logging and analysis tools.
  • You define and execute integration and system-level tests on real robots, test benches, and in simulation.
  • You shape and drive the adoption of AI-assisted engineering practices across the team, from coding and test generation to AI-supported log analysis.
  • You develop technical concepts and architectures for robot control, analyze requirements and trade-offs, and align design decisions with system architects, safety experts, and navigation specialists.
  • You drive cross-team initiatives and mentor colleagues, depending on your experience and expertise.

Requirements

  • You hold a degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Computer Science, Robotics, or a related field, or bring equivalent practical experience.
  • You bring at least 6 years of professional experience in robotics software development, including at least 3 years working with real mobile robots.
  • You actively use AI-based tools, such as coding assistants, in your daily work and are eager to explore their potential further.
  • You have proven experience developing technical concepts and architectures for robotic systems.
  • You have a solid understanding of mobile robot kinematics, including acceleration-limited motion, and how localization and navigation interact with the hardware.
  • You bring extensive experience with ROS1/ROS2 or comparable middleware, as well as ros_control/ros2_control or similar frameworks.
  • You have experience integrating sensors, actuators, and fieldbus systems, ideally CANopen.
  • You have strong programming skills in C++ and solid knowledge of Python. Experience with Rust is a plus.
  • You bring in-depth expertise in at least one of the following areas:
    • Safety PLC applications, such as Siemens S7 / TIA Portal Safety, Beckhoff TwinSAFE, or SICK Flexi Soft.
    • Low-level, hardware-related software development, including CAN drivers, PROFINET, timing, and synchronization in sensor networks, ideally combined with microcontroller or embedded systems knowledge.
    • Autonomous software for real robots, such as localization, navigation, and motion planning, combined with an interest in developing deeper expertise in low-level control.
  • You are passionate about developing software that enables heavy autonomous vehicles to move smoothly and safely, and want to help shape the future of large robotic fleets in real warehouse environments.
  • You ideally have experience with jerk-limited motion, setting up complete mobile robot software stacks, or intralogistics applications involving automated forklifts, AGVs, or AMRs.
  • You communicate fluently in English and have intermediate German language skills (B1 level or higher).
  • You are willing to work on-site at our Munich location.

What we have to offer

  • Cutting-edge technology: As pioneers in robotics we can navigate and manipulate without rails and guides and offer solutions to processes that no one could automate ever before!
  • Team: We are an international team with more than 25 nationalities. You’ll work in a team with exceptionally smart, humble, collaborative and hardworking individuals.
  • Culture: Come as you are! Join a vibrant, inventive, and diverse team that values collaboration over hierarchy. To innovate you need to fail from time to time — we always learn and improve.
  • Workplace: Our office is located near the S‑Bahn station “Hirschgarten”. We work in a loft-style office with great equipment, our own workshop and testing area.
  • Full Board: You don’t feel like thinking about what you want to have for lunch tomorrow, not to mention preparing it? Luckily, our french cook treats us with a freshly cooked free lunch everyday! And as the cherry on top, there is a packed fridge with drinks, fresh fruits and of course coffee!
  • Flexibility: Flexibility is a top priority for us. Our hybrid working model for positions where presence is dispensable helps to achieve a healthy work-life balance.
  • Benefits: We offer attractive holiday, EGYM, health care, and compensation packages. Learn more about our current benefits here.

Not sure if you meet every single requirement? That's okay. We know that great people don't always tick every box. If you're excited about the opportunity to help shape the future of robotics and believe you can make an impact, we'd love to hear from you. Your experience may be a great fit for this role or another opportunity at Jungheinrich Robotics.

At Jungheinrich Robotics, where Magazino GmbH found its place, fostering inclusivity is very important to us. We are dedicated to create an inclusive environment for all candidates and provide equal opportunities to all qualified applicants regardless of gender, ethnicity, age, national origin, sexual orientation, culture, or education. If you need any reasonable adjustments to make the application process accessible for you, we’ll do our best to accommodate you. Feel free to approach us for that!

title: Stage Communication – Stratégie de communication innovante (Adopt AI)
descriptionHtml:
Durée : 6 mois – Temps plein
Période : à partir de février 2027
Localisation : Paris 9e
Encadré par : la responsable communication de l’événement

À propos d’Adopt AI – Grand Palais

Du 30 novembre et 2 décembre 2027, Artefact Open Innovation organise la 4ᵉ édition d’Adopt AI – Grand Palais, le sommet international de référence dédié à l’intelligence artificielle.

Organisé au Grand Palais à Paris, l’événement réunira plus de 20 000 participants, 800 intervenants et 250 exposants.
Son ambition est triple :

  • Inspirer, grâce à des intervenants internationaux de renom partageant leur vision

  • Montrer concrètement comment l’IA transforme les industries à travers des retours d’expérience

  • Mobiliser les écosystèmes autour de discussions concrètes pour accélérer l’adoption réelle de l’IA

À propos d’Artefact Open Innovation

Chez Artefact Open Innovation, nous sommes des entrepreneurs convaincus que la compétitivité, l’efficacité et la transformation des grandes organisations se gagnent en développant de nouvelles formes de collaborations et une compréhension des enjeux liés à l’adoption des nouvelles technologies – notamment DATA et IA.

Pour cela, nous partageons et propageons l’esprit entrepreneur avec des modes de collaboration plus agiles à l’échelle :

  • Des individus, à travers des programmes de formation et l’accélération de projets d’innovation

Missions

En soutien direct à la chargée de communication et au sein du pôle événementiel & communication, vous interviendrez sur un large spectre de missions :

Communication et stratégie de marque

  • Participation à la réflexion autour de la promotion de l’évènement Adopt AI - Grand Palais
  • Contribution à la cohérence des messages et des prises de parole sur l’ensemble des supports
  • Appui à la structuration de la stratégie de communication de l’événement
  • Réflexion autour de l’amélioration du SEO et du référencement de notre site internet et nos réseaux sociaux, clean et qualification de la base de données

Création de contenus

  • Création de visuels sur Canva
  • Réalisation de formats vidéos courts (teasers, annonces, formats réseaux sociaux)
  • Création de kits de communication à destination des partenaires et intervenants
  • Rédaction de posts LinkedIn et de contenus éditoriaux liés à l’événement

Mailings & diffusion

  • Rédaction et envoi de mailings marketing ciblés
  • Contribution à la diffusion des contenus auprès des différents écosystèmes (entreprises, institutions, startups, IA)

Partenariats

  • Appui au suivi des contreparties partenaires
  • Contribution à la structuration de packages de communication

Contribution à la réflexion stratégique

  • Participation aux brainstormings autour :
    • de nouveaux formats de contenus
    • de nouveaux canaux de communication

  • Contribution à la réflexion sur :
    • le choix des prestataires photo / vidéo
    • la mise en place d’un rétroplanning de communication
    • Des campagnes publicitaires (web)
    • Des campagnes Linkedin Ads

Le ou la stagiaire sera force de proposition et impliqué·e dans la réflexion, les décisions finales relevant de la responsable communication.

Profil recherché

  • Étudiant·e en Master communication, marketing ou équivalent
  • Intérêt marqué pour l’IA et l’événementiel
  • Sensibilité aux enjeux de positionnement, de message et de cohérence éditoriale
  • Excellente orthographe en français et bilingue anglais (pour suivre et participer à l’écrit et à l’oral dans les deux langues)
  • Organisé·e, rigoureux·se, à l’aise avec la gestion de projets
  • Autonome, curieux·se, force de proposition

Compétences techniques

  • Canva indispensable
  • Outils de montage vidéo appréciés
  • Connaissance d’outils de mailing (Pardot ou autre)

Conditions

  • Gratification : selon profil et convention
  • Lieu : Paris 9e, avec possibilité de télétravail partiel

title: Strategy & Operations Director
descriptionHtml:
About Doit

We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, accessible and safe.

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who love building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who care about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society.

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it’s the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

The Role

Doit is building its investment business from Vilnius. As Strategy & Operations Lead of Doit Lithuania, you will build and run the business in Lithuania and grow it across the European Economic Area.

You will be the first senior hire in Lithuania. You will own the regulatory relationship, the build of the team, the partner network and the launch. You will sit on the management board and lead the business day to day.

We’re looking for a generalist who learns quickly, thinks deeply, and enjoys solving difficult problems in a fast-moving, regulated environment.

What You’ll Own

  • Own the relationship with the Bank of Lithuania and other regulators.

  • Build the Vilnius team, including compliance, operations and control functions.

  • Select and negotiate with execution, custody, fund and banking partners.

  • Own the business plan, financial projections, capital plan and budget.

  • Launch the investment platform in Lithuania and roll it out across the EEA.

  • Set up governance, policies and controls that meet EU and Lithuanian requirements.

  • Work with group leadership on product, engineering and growth.

  • Report to the board and take ownership of business and regulatory outcomes.

What We’re Looking For

  • Generalist background in consulting, investment banking, start-ups, private equity or venture capital.

  • Experience building or scaling a business, ideally in financial services or fintech.

  • Strong problem-solving skills and business judgment.

  • Ability to learn regulation quickly and work credibly with regulators.

  • Strong ownership and execution skills.

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with boards, regulators, partners and teams.

  • Comfortable working across product, operations, finance and compliance.

  • A clean record and good reputation, suitable for regulatory approval as a senior manager.

  • Based in Lithuania, or open to relocating to Lithuania.

  • Curious, resourceful, and driven to build.

Nice to Have

  • Lithuanian language ability.

  • An existing working relationship with the Bank of Lithuania.

  • Experience with MiFID II, brokerage, wealth management or fund distribution.

  • Experience building or running a regulated financial business in the EU.

This Role Is Not For

  • People who only want to attend meetings.

  • Candidates who cannot follow up aggressively and professionally.

  • Those who need fixed scope and slow timelines.

  • People who avoid messy cross-functional problems.

  • People who produce long updates without clear decisions or next actions.

  • People who see regulation as someone else’s problem.

Location

This role is based in Vilnius, Lithuania. This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our Vilnius office at least 3 days per week.

You must be a European citizen or already hold a valid right to work in Lithuania. We are not able to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Role-specific interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process.

Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritised.

title: System Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About Invisix

Semiconductor manufacturers can't build what they can't measure. Invisix Measuring Systems is a fast-growing scale-up in the high-tech industry, developing next-generation metrology solutions for the semiconductor sector. We work at the intersection of optics, software, and data.

We're a small team, but the depth of knowledge inside Invisix is anything but small. Our culture is professional and fast-paced, with short communication lines and a strong sense of shared purpose. Everyone here is committed, and everyone knows their work directly contributes to something bigger.

The Role

We're looking for a System Engineer to make our metrology equipment work to spec in a real program: requirements, error budgets, integration and verification, and system-level problem solving amongst others.

Reporting to our CTO, you take a program or release of our product, or a subsystem of it, from requirements to a tool that passes customer acceptance and ships on time. You work with our module and discipline engineers, integration, quality and service, and you're the technical contact for customers on specifications, acceptance criteria and escalations. Our system architect owns the concept; you make it work and prove it. The role includes occasional travel to customers in Asia, the US and Europe.

Key Responsibilities

  • Break down system requirements into module requirements, and keep them traceable from customer need to test result

  • Own the detailed error budgets, and update them with measured data as the system matures

  • Write and maintain the interface control documents between modules, together with the module and discipline engineers

  • Set up integration, test, verification and qualification plans, and make sure the tool passes customer acceptance

  • Find the root cause of system-level problems across disciplines, and stay in contact with the factory and the field after shipment

  • Agree specifications and acceptance criteria with the system architect, handle technical escalations, and take on adjacent responsibilities as the company grows, such as system engineering for a next product release

Is this you?

  • MSc or PhD in physics, applied physics, mechatronics, electrical engineering or a related field, with at least 5 years of experience in system engineering for complex high-tech equipment

  • Experience in semiconductor equipment, for example lithography, metrology or inspection, or in comparable high-tech equipment

  • A solid physics background, especially in optics or measurement physics, so you can understand and quantify what limits system performance

  • Hands-on experience with requirements breakdown and traceability, error budgets, and integration, verification and qualification plans

  • Experience with model-based systems engineering (MBSE), for example with SysML

  • A rigorous, data-driven and systematic way of working, and enough depth in several disciplines to debug across them

  • Active use of AI tooling in your daily work (requirements analysis, data analysis, test reporting, documentation) to boost efficiency

Nice to have

title: System Test Automation Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our Verification and Release Test Team

Wayve’s Verification and Release Test team sits at the intersection of hardware, embedded software and machine learning models. Our testing spans component, system and vehicle levels, and we build novel test automation in-house to identify issues earlier in development. We pride ourselves on finding the most efficient and effective ways to deliver the most valuable results for the company.

As a System Test Engineer, HIL, you’ll build robust, reusable automation and work across engineering disciplines to improve coverage, reliability and traceability. This is a hands-on delivery role with room to grow into broader areas of the system, including sensing and model-behaviour testing, as Wayve and your experience evolve.

🧠 Your day-to-day

  • Develop automation for system functionality tests at component, integration and system levels, working across software and hardware boundaries.

  • Lead root-cause investigations for failures identified during test campaigns, collaborating with hardware, software, infrastructure and DevOps teams to resolve issues.

  • Analyse test results, uncover software and hardware bugs, and report findings through Jira with clear evidence to support debugging.

  • Optimise Buildkite CI/CD-integrated test workflows for rapid, reliable and repeatable execution.

  • Review, create and follow risk assessments to ensure all testing activities are conducted safely and responsibly.

🧩 What you’ll be working on:

  • Independently owning the design and delivery of automated verification for a defined area of our embedded software stack, steadily raising the bar on coverage, reliability and traceability.

  • Building open-loop and closed-loop hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) replay tests, alongside reliability and fault-injection tests, to support verification, release and debugging.

  • Automating HIL test setups and improving test infrastructure to expand coverage, make failures easier to trace and strengthen compliance reporting.

  • Integrating requirements, coverage and compliance workflows, including Jama, MC/DC coverage analysis and MISRA checks, and managing test artefacts through Artifactory and Azure.

  • Developing traceability dashboards and defining KPIs and quality metrics that support data-driven validation and release decisions.

🙌 You should apply if:

  • You have hands-on experience with system-level verification and validation in robotics, embedded software or mechatronic systems, with a track record of independently delivering test automation.

  • You’re highly proficient in Python and have experience developing automation test frameworks using pytest.

  • You’ve worked with HIL testing and tooling, including interfaces such as CAN, Ethernet or GMSL, and tools from dSPACE, Vector, Xylon or similar providers.

  • You understand open-loop and closed-loop HIL replay testing using dSPACE or other emulators.

  • You’re familiar with automotive safety and process standards, including ISO 26262, ASPICE and SOTIF, and have experience integrating requirements and test-management tools such as Jama and Xray.

  • You’re proficient in CI/CD principles and related tooling, such as GitLab CI, Buildkite and Bazel.

  • You have experience developing or testing automotive software at embedded and system levels, including hardware/software interactions and interface-level testing, and have worked with L2+ hands-off, L3 or L4 automated driving systems.

  • You have knowledge of consumer safety-rating protocols such as Euro NCAP, including AEB and LSS/LKA scenarios; DCAS regulatory testing under UN R171; and automotive cybersecurity testing and standards, including ISO/SAE 21434 and UN R155.

  • You’ve worked with test automation dashboards, logging and reporting infrastructure, using tools such as Grafana, Looker, Datadog and Jira.

  • You’re a self-starter with a sharp eye for improvement who communicates clearly and works effectively across software, hardware, autonomy, DevOps and product teams.

  • Ideally, you’ve contributed to improvements in test methods, safety procedures or operational efficiency, and are familiar with data management and version control tools such as Git.

  • Experience using agentic AI coding tools such as Cursor or Claude Code to accelerate and improve test development, debugging and automation workflows would also be valuable.

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

More about Wayve:

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

🔍 The Interview Process:

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

  • Initial call / recruiter screen (30 minutes)

  • Competency Interviews (Programming and hiring manager interview; 1 hour 45 minutes total)

  • Deep-dive technical interviews (Cross-functional, system design; 1 hour 45 minutes total)

  • Final interview: mission & values alignment (45 minutes).

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

What’s in it for you (Location dependant):

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually
✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs
📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth
🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more

A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law.

For more information visit Careers at Wayve. To learn more about what drives us, visit Values at Wayve

DISCLAIMER: We will not ask about marriage or pregnancy, care responsibilities or disabilities in any of our job adverts or interviews. However, we do look to capture information about care responsibilities, and disabilities among other diversity information as part of an optional DEI Monitoring form to help us identify areas of improvement in our hiring process and ensure that the process is inclusive and non-discriminatory.

title: Talent Acquisition Intern
descriptionHtml:
Talent Acquisition Intern

Deine Mission bei trawa

Bei trawa sind wir überzeugt: Die Energiewende beginnt bei den Menschen, die sie möglich machen. Du willst leistungsstarke Teams mit aufbauen und Recruiting von Grund auf so lernen, dass es wirklich Wirkung hat? Dann bist du bei trawa genau richtig.

Als Talent Acquisition Intern bist du das operative Rückgrat unseres Talent-Teams und sorgst mit uns dafür, dass die richtigen Menschen zu trawa finden. Du hältst unsere Prozesse am Laufen, gestaltest reibungslose Candidate Journeys, räumst administrative Hürden aus dem Weg und hilfst, ein Hiring-Erlebnis zu bauen, das hängen bleibt. So bringst du direkt mit voran, was uns antreibt: Unternehmen den Zugang zu echter, grüner Energie zu ermöglichen.

Diese Rolle passt perfekt zu dir, wenn du Talent Acquisition hands-on lernen willst, gerne mit modernen Tools und KI-Lösungen arbeitest und direkt sehen möchtest, wie dein Beitrag das gesamte Team schneller und besser macht.

Bei uns findest du keine starren Strukturen - dafür Gestaltungsspielraum, Vertrauen und ein Team, das die Energiewende gemeinsam voranbringt.

Wir freuen uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen!

Was du bei uns vorantreibst

Du hilfst dabei, die Zukunft der Energiebranche mitzugestalten – und übernimmst Verantwortung für Themen, die echten Impact haben: auf unsere Hiring-Qualität, unsere Kultur und unser Wachstum. title: Talent Partner
descriptionHtml:
Build the team that builds Conveo. As our London Talent Partner, you'll source and close top talent across the UK, US and Belgium as we scale past 100 people.

Conveo is a Y Combinator-backed company in an active growth period. We're scaling past 100 people and delivering our 2027 hiring plan. The people who join now have an outsized chance to shape how this company is built.

We raised a $50M Series A led by DST Global, giving us the fuel to move even faster. We're investing in our product, growing an exceptional team, and taking on bigger challenges as we enter our next stage of growth.

What We’re Building

Conveo is the AI research platform enabling fast, affordable, and high-quality consumer and B2B research. Global brands like Unilever, Google, and Canva use our AI video interviewer to generate insights across marketing and product teams.

Traditional research is slow, expensive, and superficial. Running it well requires expertise most teams don't have. That gap affects how well companies understand their customers and how well they can serve them. We're closing it.

The Role

As Talent Partner at Conveo, you will build the team that builds the company. You'll join a small, lean talent team and play a big part in how we scale. You'll play a key part in how Conveo attracts, assesses, and ultimately hires talent across the US, UK, and Belgium, helping us scale past 100 people and deliver our 2027 hiring plan.

You'll close exceptional talent across engineering, product, go-to-market, and operations, while contributing to hiring strategy and talent decisions. You won't be limited to one area. You'll work with stakeholders and leadership across departments. If your experience leans towards one area, such as product and engineering, go-to-market, or operations, that's fine. We're open to candidates with a variety of backgrounds.

This isn't a transactional recruiting role. You'll shape how candidates experience Conveo and help build a team with high talent density for the long term. Proactive sourcing and strong execution will be central to your success.

Talent operations plays a small part in this role. Lots of foundations are already in place, and you'll help build on them as we scale. If you like to experiment and work with the latest tech, especially AI, you'll find this role really interesting.

We're growing fast, so priorities shift and you'll often make calls with imperfect information.

What You’ll Do

Own hiring outcomes end-to-end

  • Partner closely with hiring managers and leadership

  • Own roles from kickoff to close, including sourcing and closing

  • Maintain speed without sacrificing quality

  • Develop strong hiring judgment

Build proactive talent pipelines

  • Develop centralised talent pipelines across key disciplines, enabling the business to take a broader and more proactive approach to hiring

  • Create innovative sourcing strategies for particular searches, incorporating AI-enabled sourcing, targeted outbound campaigns, market mapping, events, and external communities

  • Proactively source top-tier talent using LinkedIn, Juicebox, and other tools. Our toolkit isn't fixed. We're always looking at new tools, and deciding whether to build them internally or use them externally, to level up our sourcing and recruitment capabilities.

  • Provide external talent intelligence, including candidate availability, competitor activity, compensation, and wider market trends

Build a high-signal candidate experience

  • Be the main point of contact and advocate for candidates

  • Every candidate hears back from us quickly, whether it's a yes or a no.

  • Pitch Conveo with real conviction, because you understand the product, the market and why people join.

Grow our employer brand

  • Contribute to employer branding content that shows what it's like to work at Conveo

  • Support events that put Conveo in front of top talent

Build scalable hiring and people systems

  • Improve interview loops, scorecards, and decision-making

  • Track funnel health

  • Maintain clean hiring and people data in Ashby (our ATS) and internal tools

  • Build repeatable playbooks and templates

What Success Looks Like

  • Hiring managers see you as a true partner and want you on their searches: you've added key players to their teams quickly and efficiently.

  • Hires that work out: you bring in the right people, and we can see who was hired and why they did well in the organisation.

  • Ownership of our hiring goals: you understand the hiring plan and your contribution to it. When blockers come up, you flag them and proactively work to fix them so we hit our goals.

  • Gaps found and closed: you work autonomously, but take time early on to understand what gaps exist and why, then work with the team to close them.

  • Better decisions over time: you make decisions in the moment with the best information available, even when the data isn't perfect, and push to gather more data so future decisions are better informed.

  • A better way of doing things: you challenge the status quo when something could be done in a way that's better for the business, drawing on your experience and backing it up with data and resources.

Your First 3 Months

  • You've taken ownership of a set of live roles and closed your first few hires.

  • You've built a pipeline for our hardest-to-hire discipline, so we're ahead of demand, not chasing it.

  • Hiring managers trust you as a partner and come to you early when they're planning hires.

What You’ll Bring

You're truth first, not fluff first: opinionated and thoughtful, with high standards and low ego. You're structured, fast, and iterative, and you build things once and make them reusable. You'll also bring:

  • Minimum 4 years of recruiting or high-performance hiring experience across in-house teams, startups, scale-ups, or agencies

  • Excellent proactive sourcing, headhunting, and market-mapping skills, with the ability to engage high-performing passive candidates who aren't actively seeking a move

  • Strong execution and high ownership: you run several roles and priorities at once, keep every process moving without dropped steps, and follow through on what you commit to

  • A good understanding of recruitment analytics and the ability to use data to influence hiring strategy and improve performance

  • Practical experience using AI and modern recruitment technology to improve sourcing, personalisation, market intelligence, and recruitment efficiency

  • Experience partnering closely with senior leaders, and the ability to build credibility with highly senior stakeholders

  • A builder mentality and a genuine interest in tech, AI, and the startup community. You enjoy identifying problems, improving processes, and creating better ways of working rather than simply operating within an existing recruitment model.

Why Join Us?

  • Build the team for a hyper-growth, YC-backed AI company

  • Work directly with founders and strong operators. At our size, every hire you make visibly shapes the company.

  • Competitive salary and equity.

  • Based in our London office 3 days a week. We also have offices in Antwerp and New York.

  • Regular socials: rooftop drinks, team dinners, run clubs, and more

  • Twice-yearly off-sites to places worth travelling to: Austria, Las Vegas, and Portugal

  • Private health coverage with Vitality (incl. dental, vision)

  • Enhanced employer pension contribution (5% employer, 3% employee contribution)

  • Refer someone great and earn up to £5,000

title: Tax Operations Intern
descriptionHtml:

Founded in 2025, Taxforce rethinks tax advisory from the ground up: AI-powered and highly automated, yet personal. We're starting with healthcare professionals, a complex and underserved segment, and we grow both organically and through M&A.

This is a €40B market in Germany alone, with processes that have barely changed in decades. AI now enables a fundamental shift, and there are no playbooks yet. We're writing them. We're a small, highly ambitious team in Berlin, backed by €5M from Tenet VC and founded by alumni of Goldman Sachs, Harvard Business School, Bain & Company, Y Combinator and the former Klarna Head of Engineering.

The role

You work right in the middle of our tax work for doctors’ and dentists’ practices. You support our tax advisors on live mandates from day one. Because tech and tax work together at Taxforce, you also help turn manual steps into automation.

Tasks

  • Ongoing bookkeeping. Prepare financial accounting for our practices in DATEV: receipt capture, booking, account reconciliation.

  • Year-end and returns. Prepare annual financial statement packages and give draft-level input on tax returns, with feedback from our tax advisors.

  • Deadlines and documents. Support our digital mail and tax-assessment processing, deadline control and client master data.

  • Client communication. Run structured document requests and follow-ups with our practices.

  • Automation. Test our internal tools and help automate recurring steps such as document classification and data extraction.

Requirements

  • Relevant studies. You’re studying business, economics, law, tax or a related field, with a strong interest in tax and accounting.

  • First practical experience. You’ve worked in a tax firm, accounting or audit, as an intern, working student or trained Steuerfachangestellte/r.

  • Care & accuracy. You work carefully and precisely, because in tax every detail counts.

  • Structured & independent. You organise yourself well and get things done without everything spelled out.

  • Tech-savvy. You use AI tools comfortably and enjoy building small automations. DATEV experience is a plus.

  • German language skills. Our clients speak German, so we require fluent German (C2) and good English.

Benefits

  • Learn hands-on from tax advisors. Work side by side with experienced tax advisors on real mandates, with direct feedback and mentoring.

  • Ownership from day one. Take on real responsibility in live client work early on.

  • Front-row seat to AI in the real world. See how AI changes the daily work of a tax firm and help build it.

  • Healthcare insight. Understand how medical and dental practices work financially, a segment few tax firms truly know.

  • A path to stay. Strong interns get an offer to continue as working student or full-time.

The details

Full-time internship for 3 to 6 months, start any time of the year, on-site in our Berlin office five days a week.

How to apply

Send us your CV and a few lines on why this role fits you. Our process has three steps: a 30-minute intro call, a short live case from our day-to-day work, and a conversation with the founders.
